dec8faf6c7e5c205: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's key index opened higher on Monday before easing marginally in early trade, amid continued buying interest following Wall Street's stronger performance and easing United States-China trade tensions, an analyst said.
At 9.10am, the benchmark index eased 0.10 of-a-point, or 0.006 per cent, to 1,671.52 from Friday's close of 1,671.62.
The index opened 0.93 of-a-point higher at 1,672.55.
Market breadth was negative, with losers outnumbering gainers 226 to 153. A total of 332 counters were unchanged, while 2,213 were untraded and 91 suspended.
Turnover stood at 209.81 million shares worth RM115.48 million.
aec4e0ac494cf3f2: KLANG: Three vehicles, including a motorcycle, were destroyed in an early morning fire at Block B of Apartment Meru Impian in Kapar, near here, today.
In the 5.07am incident, a Proton Exora multi-purpose vehicle was 80 per cent burnt, a Toyota Vios was 60 per cent damaged, while a Yamaha Avantiz motorcycle was 30 per cent burnt.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said a team from the Kapar Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call.
"Firefighters arrived at the scene at 5.11am, about four minutes after receiving the distress call.

"The operation commander reported that the fire involved three vehicles, and firefighters immediately carried out extinguishing operations using a hose reel line connected to the fire engine's water tank," he said in a statement today.
Ashrul Riezal said five firefighters using one fire engine brought the blaze under control by 5.50am, before fully wrapping up the operation at 6.20am.
He said no casualties were reported, and the cause of the fire is under investigation.
813513727be3e3d2: LOS ANGELES: Madonna and Sabrina Carpenter claimed best collaboration and K-pop superstar Lisa won best pop video as MTV kicked off its annual Video Music Awards on Sunday.

"Bring Your Love" from Madonna and Carpenter earned the VMA collaboration award at the show in downtown Los Angeles. The pair had opened the ceremony with a high-energy performance of the song to the cheering crowd.
Madonna, the night's top nominee, said she enjoyed working with Carpenter because their work styles complemented each other.

"When I show up late, she shows up early," Madonna said, adding that both share the old-school habit of writing lyrics on pieces of paper. "It's been wonderful working with you, and I love this song," she added.

Lisa, a member of the group Blackpink, won the VMA for best pop video for her solo effort "Dream." Sporting a black outfit with large white fringe sleeves, she spoke through tears as she thanked her fans, known as Lillies.
"I wouldn't be here without you guys," she said as she held the VMA Moon Person trophy. "Thank you so much for your love and support."

Taylor Swift was in attendance and was set to be awarded the inaugural MTV VMA Artist Director Honors. Swift has directed videos for many of her hits including "The Fate of Ophelia" and "All Too Well," plus the new single "Patient Zero," which was scheduled to debut during the VMAs telecast.

Swift, Madonna and Carpenter were all competing for the ceremony's top honor of video of the year. Madonna was nominated for “Confessions II - The Film," Carpenter for "Tears" and Swift for "Ophelia." Winners in the top categories are selected by fan votes.
The ceremony was broadcast live on CBS and MTV and streamed on Paramount+ PSKY.O.
054c4bf8fdb32aa6: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian government bonds came under pressure last week as rising US Treasury yields and a rebound in oil prices reversed an earlier rally, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.

The firm said Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields rose by one to four basis points week-on-week, with the 10-year yield climbing back towards four per cent after falling as low as 3.89 per cent during the week.
The 30-year MGS yield rose four basis points to 4.40 per cent, while the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (Klibor) increased three basis points to 3.51 per cent.

CIMB Securities senior economist Lim Yee Ping and research head Michelle Chia said the rise in Klibor suggested banks were building liquidity buffers ahead of the RM29.5 billion Government Investment Issues (GII) redemption on Sept 30 and quarter-end funding requirements.
The Malaysian overnight rate, meanwhile, remained at 2.75 per cent, indicating that tighter conditions were concentrated in term funding rather than overnight liquidity.
Despite the softer market, demand for the reopening of the seven-year MGS 04/33 on Sept 21 remained strong.
The RM5 billion auction attracted RM10.84 billion in bids, translating into a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.168 times, with offshore investors accounting for much of the demand.
"Demand was led by offshore accounts, with the bond offering attractive relative value against the 10-year benchmark as the seven-year to 10-year spread was only around two to three basis points.

"The strong auction outcome suggests that the preceding nine-week cheapening had created sufficient valuation support to attract real-money demand, although the subsequent rise in US Treasury yields has reduced some of the near-term momentum," they said in a note.
Attention now turns to the reopening of the 30-year GII 01/56 today, comprising a RM3 billion public tender and an additional RM2 billion private placement.
Lim and Chia said the auction would test investor appetite for longer-dated government debt, particularly after the sharp rise in long-end US Treasury yields.
"Sustained demand at the long end will be important for determining whether the recent steepening can be maintained," they said.
The market will also monitor Malaysia's August fiscal data, due on Sept 30, for signs of how higher oil prices are affecting the government's subsidy bill.
The figures will also indicate whether Putrajaya remains on track to meet its 2026 fiscal deficit target of 3.5 per cent ahead of the 2027 Budget on Oct 9.
Meanwhile, the Melaka state assembly was dissolved on Sept 23, triggering a state election that must be held within 60 days.
The Election Commission is scheduled to meet on Oct 7 to determine the election timetable.
"The state election adds another near-term political catalyst ahead of the broader election cycle, although the immediate market impact is likely to remain limited," they said.
Globally, US economic data will take centre stage this week as investors assess whether expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve have further room to run.

CIMB Securities said key releases include August job openings, September personal consumption expenditures inflation, the ISM manufacturing survey and, most importantly, September non-farm payrolls and wage growth.
The data, due between Sept 29 and Oct 2, will help investors assess the strength of the US economy and the outlook for further interest rate increases.
Fed officials and European Central Bank president Christine Lagarde are also scheduled to speak, while oil prices and geopolitical developments remain key risks to the inflation outlook.
Within Asean, Indonesia's September inflation and August trade data are due on Oct 1.
Thailand's Constitutional Court is also scheduled to rule today on a challenge concerning ballot secrecy in the Feb 8 election.
CIMB Securities said the ruling could have implications for the Thai government, although global oil prices and US economic data would remain key drivers across regional markets.

5145e3ff1b8163b0: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Malaysia aims to strengthen cooperation with the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) through more practical and result-oriented initiatives to address the increasingly complex threat of transnational organised crime.

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the matter was discussed during his meeting with the UNODC regional representative for South-east Asia and the Pacific on the final day of his working visit to Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (UAE), in conjunction with the 15th United Nations Congress on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice.

He said during the meeting, both sides exchanged views on the increasingly complex landscape of transnational organised crime, particularly criminal networks exploiting digital technology to expand their activities across borders and jurisdictions.

“As a country strategically located in the heart of Asean, Malaysia takes these developments seriously. Our approach involves not only integrated enforcement but also prevention, cutting off illicit financial flows and strengthening regional and international cooperation,” he said in a statement posted on his social media page yesterday.

Elaborating, Saifuddin Nasution said the discussions also focused on efforts to tackle cyber-enabled organised crime, the illicit trafficking of people and contraband, as well as the misuse of emerging technologies by criminal networks.
He said Malaysia recognised the importance of UNODC continuing to support Asean countries through regional capacity building, information sharing and exchange of best practices.

“Cross-border threats continue to evolve and expand, and strong cooperation networks with regional and international partners are an important part of our efforts to ensure Malaysia’s security remains safeguarded,” he said. — Bernama
907e5a518b4b6bd8: PUTRAJAYA: Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M Saravanan and several family members arrived at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) headquarters here today, believed to be to receive asset declaration notices
Saravanan arrived at the MACC headquarters entrance at 9.15am with his wife and two children in two black Toyota Alphard and Vellfire vehicles.

He is facing three charges of allegedly accepting RM1.097 million in bribes four years ago in connection with the approval of an application for 1,000 foreign worker quotas for TYKB Engineering Sdn Bhd.
Saravanan, who is also MIC deputy president, pleaded not guilty to the charges at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court on Aug 28.
On Friday, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said he will serve asset declaration notices on Saravanan, his wife and three children.
a452b20fd3e2b297: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Police are investigating a case of vandalism and voluntarily causing hurt after a car collided with several parked vehicles and a related assault, which went viral on TikTok.

Ampang Jaya district police chief ACP Khairul Anuar Khalid said in a statement today that the incident happened on September 26 at about 7am, when the complainant picked up a female friend, identified only as Nadia, from her home to go hiking at Bukit Melati, Nilai.

After the hike, the complainant drove Nadia home to Pangsapuri Sri Intan. There, the complainant was approached by three men, one of whom knocked on the driver's-side window and told the complainant to get out.
The complainant, who did not know the men, became frightened and accelerated forward, hitting several cars parked at the location.
The statement said one of the men then stood on the car's bonnet and was struck by three unidentified men in front of Orkid Apartment. The incident was later shared widely on TikTok.

Police are investigating under Section 427 of the Penal Code for mischief causing loss or damage, which carries a jail term of up to five years, a fine, or both. They are also investigating under Section 323 for voluntarily causing hurt, which carries up to one year in jail, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both.
Khairul Anuar urged members of the public with information on the case to come forward to assist investigators. He also advised the public not to speculate about the incident.

9c550a463866c8bb: KOTA BARU: The Road Transport Department (RTD) has detected businesses hiring foreigners to drive lorries and buses, as well as Malaysians renting motorcycles to foreigners for profit.
RTD senior enforcement director Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said the operators were flouting the law to cut costs and increase profits.
He said foreigners were not eligible to apply for Goods Driving Licence (GDL) or Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licences to drive goods or public service vehicles.

"Business operators should not collude with foreigners by hiring them to drive lorries or buses. They should not compromise safety and the law simply to increase profits," he told reporters yesterday.
Kifli said Malaysians who rented out their vehicles to foreigners, particularly motorcycles, were also contributing to the problem.
"Foreigners without valid documents are not allowed to drive or own vehicles on Malaysian roads. If they cannot legally own or use these vehicles, how can they drive them?
"This happens because Malaysians rent out their vehicles to foreigners. As long as some collude with them, foreigners will continue to use vehicles freely on our roads," he said.
He urged vehicle owners to stop renting out their vehicles to foreigners.
Kifli said the RTD issued 481,119 summonses from 2024 to September this year — 183,300 in 2024, 191,676 in 2025 and 106,143 from January to September this year.
The offences included driving without a Competent Driving Licence (CDL), expired motor vehicle licences (LKM), lack of insurance and other road traffic offences.
He said the department had adopted a stricter approach, with both the foreigner driving the vehicle and its owner being issued summonses.
"Neither the driver nor the vehicle owner will be allowed to settle the compound, and the cases will have to be brought to court," he said.
Kifli said stern action would also be taken against companies that hired foreigners to drive commercial vehicles.
"The lorry or bus driven by a foreigner can be forfeited. This action has been carried out over the past three months as the issue has become increasingly prevalent.
"This is done under the provisions of the Land Public Transport Act (Apad), as it involves commercial vehicles," he said.
For private vehicles, he said most cases were brought to court, while forfeiture proceedings could also be initiated if vehicle owners failed to appear in court.
Under Section 23(2) of the Road Transport Act 1987, a person convicted of an offence can be fined between RM1,000 and RM10,000, or jailed for up to two years, or both.
Kifli said Rohingya were among those most frequently found riding motorcycles, followed by Pakistanis and Indonesians.
For lorries, he said Bangladeshis, Indonesians and Indians were among the foreigners found driving them.
He said motorcycles were commonly rented to foreigners for RM50 to RM200 a month, depending on their condition.
"Three-wheeled motorcycles are particularly common on the East Coast and are usually used to collect discarded or recyclable materials, with many operated by Rohingya citizens," he said.

c7502c22ad4c1361: ISTANBUL: Spain defeated defending champions North Korea 4-3 on penalties on Sunday to win the FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup in Lodz, Poland, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
The final at Stadion Miejski LKS Lodz ended goalless after 90 minutes and extra time before Spain goalkeeper Lopez emerged as the hero in the shootout, saving efforts from Choe Yon-A and Pak Il-Sim.

The hotly contested match saw both sides create chances, with Lopez producing a crucial intervention in the first half after Ho Kyong collected the ball outside the penalty area following a mistake by the Spanish defence.
Spain upped the pressure after the break, with Pau Comendador forcing a diving save from North Korean goalkeeper Pak Ju-Gyong in the 78th minute.
After the match went into extra time, Spain forward Marisa Garcia twice came close to breaking the deadlock, but Pak denied her on both occasions.
Lopez then completed her decisive performance in the shootout as Spain secured their second U-20 Women's World Cup title after their 2022 triumph in Costa Rica.
The victory also gave Spain their second global women's youth title in succession.
The final was a repeat of the 2024 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup decider, when North Korea defeated Spain 4-3 on penalties.
Several players from that match featured again in Lodz, giving Spain an opportunity to overturn their previous defeat.
North Korea had entered the final after an unbeaten campaign in which they won every match without conceding a goal, having also claimed both the U-17 and U-20 world titles in 2024. — BERNAMA

361e26601f70006a: JERUSALEM, Sept 28 — Israeli media reported today that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had made an unannounced visit to the United Arab Emirates to meet with the Gulf state’s leader.
TV channels 12 and KAN as well as the newspapers Haaretz and The Jerusalem Post said that Netanyahu undertook a one-day visit to the UAE to meet President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
The premier’s office did not immediately comment.
The reported visit comes with the Middle East still gripped by the Israel-US war launched against Iran in February.

It also comes weeks after a bombshell Israeli media report that said the Emirati president warned Netanyahu ahead of Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, which the Israeli premier did not pass on to the security services.
Israel and the UAE formally established diplomatic relations in 2020 as part of the US-negotiated Abraham Accords. — AFP
349bb6b1dfc00623: PETALING JAYA: Kedudukan Rashidi Zinol sebagai satu-satunya Exco Barisan Nasional (BN) dalam kerajaan Pulau Pinang dilihat tersepit dalam ketegangan antara Umno dan Pakatan Harapan (PH), walaupun kerjasama dalam pentadbiran negeri dikatakan berjalan baik.
Syaza Shukri dari Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia (UIAM) berkata masalah sebenar terletak pada krisis kepercayaan yang masih wujud antara kedua-dua pihak.
Menurutnya, keadaan itu berbeza dengan kerjasama di peringkat pentadbiran, yang boleh berjalan tanpa bermaksud hubungan politik antara parti sudah benar-benar stabil.
"Walaupun mentadbir bersama dengan baik tetapi mereka masih belum sampai ke tahap di mana kepercayaan antara kedua-dua pihak itu benar-benar kukuh," katanya kepada FMT.
Rashidi sebelum ini menggesa kerjasama BN-PH di Pulau Pinang diteruskan, dengan berkata beliau tidak menghadapi masalah bekerjasama dengan pemimpin PKR dan DAP sepanjang tiga tahun menjadi Exco.

Pengerusi jawatankuasa pembangunan luar bandar, agro­teknologi, keterjaminan makanan dan keusahawanan Pulau Pinang itu menyifatkan hubungan berkenaan sebagai membina dan memberi manfaat kepada negeri.

Adun Sungai Acheh itu juga berharap kerjasama berkenaan dapat dikekalkan sehingga akhir penggal pada 12 Ogos 2028, namun berkata beliau bersedia menerima apa juga keputusan parti dan PH mengenai kedudukannya.

Bagaimanapun, Ketua Pemuda Umno Pulau Pinang Hilmi Elias kemudian menjelaskan gesaan Rashidi itu hanya pandangan peribadi dan bukan pendirian rasmi Umno negeri, yang belum membuat keputusan mengenai hala tuju kerjasama politiknya.
Hubungan kedua-dua parti di Pulau Pinang menjadi tegang selepas beberapa kenyataan pemimpin Umno terhadap PH dan DAP, termasuk ketika Perhimpunan Agung Umno, awal bulan ini.
Sebelum ini, Penasihat DAP Lim Guan Eng menggesa Umno disingkirkan daripada kerajaan Pulau Pinang selepas BN menjalinkan kerjasama dengan Perikatan Nasional (PN) di Negeri Sembilan.
Timbalan Pengerusi PH Pulau Pinang Faiz Fadzil berkata kedudukan Umno dalam kerajaan negeri perlu dibincangkan kerana keadaan hubungan mereka sudah berubah.
Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri dari Global Asia Consulting pula berkata keadaan itu menggambarkan satu “paradoks politik” yang sedang dihadapi Umno.
“Di pentas parti, PH sering ditembak. Tetapi di kerusi kerajaan, kerjasama dengan PH masih mahu dipertahankan.
“Inilah wajah Umno hari ini, bukan tidak tahu ke mana mahu pergi, tetapi belum cukup yakin untuk melangkah keluar,” katanya.
9b96170820590224: PETALING JAYA: An analyst sees recent statements by two Penang Umno leaders on ties with Pakatan Harapan (PH) as an indication of the party's dilemma.

Rashidi Zinol, the sole Barisan Nasional (BN) representative in the Penang government, had called for continued cooperation between the coalitions in Penang, describing it as constructive and beneficial to the state.
Penang Umno Youth chief Hilmi Elias, however, dismissed the Sungai Acheh assemblyman’s statement, saying it did not represent that of the state party leadership.
Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri of Global Asia Consulting said Umno was trying to show that it would stick to its principles, but without burning bridges with PH.
"This is where Umno’s dilemma begins. The party talks about uniting the Malays, but remains part of a PH-led government.
"Umno wants to preserve its identity, but the political reality forces it to explore every possibility," he told FMT.
BN and PH are allies at the federal level, although ties were strained following BN’s decision to join forces with Perikatan Nasional at the Negeri Sembilan state election.
Yesterday, BN chairman and Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he saw no possibility of cooperation between his coalition and PH.
Zaharuddin said BN could no longer form the government on its own following the last general election.
"So every step it takes comes with a price," he added.
Syaza Shukri of International Islamic University Malaysia said the two coalitions remained wary of each other and had yet to truly establish trust with one another.
She said while Umno had emphasised Malay unity at its general assembly, many questions among the leadership remained unanswered.
"These include whether an Umno-PAS pact would increase the party’s chances of winning at the next election," she said.
7033865ef608c982: NEW YORK, Sept 28 — Asean needs to continue strengthening connectivity among its member states as a step towards creating a more open and integrated region, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said Malaysia aspired to see Asean develop into a freer region over the next 10 to 12 years, including exploring the free movement of people, similar to that practised in the European Union (EU).
“Connectivity among Asean countries needs to be effective,” he said during a question-and-answer session at a gathering with the Malaysian diaspora here on Saturday.

Mohamad said although the aspiration could not be fully realised under current circumstances due to differences in policies and laws among member states, this should not prevent Asean from achieving the vision.
He added that the effort should be viewed as a long-term process requiring preparation and gradual change.
Meanwhile, he said Malaysia needs to prepare its people, particularly by strengthening the education system for the younger generation, to face broader competition in a more open Asean.
“Are we ready, or have we prepared our Malaysian children to compete with children from Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines and other Asean countries?” he said.
Earlier, during a joint press conference with Malaysian media, Mohamad said Asean should continue playing the role of a middle power amid global geopolitical and economic uncertainty.

He said the international community is increasingly looking towards Asean to make its voice heard because of its position as a strong bloc, its ability to articulate a more effective common position on global issues and its significant economic potential. — Bernama
98948bec88762647: SANAA, Sept 28 — Saudi airstrikes on Taiz in southwest Yemen caused dozens of casualties in an area controlled by the Houthis, the Iran-backed group said on Sunday, as fighting escalated further after a truce broke down.

The Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree accused Saudi Arabia of launching two air raids that hit a market on the outskirts of the city, saying nearly 50 people were killed or wounded without specifying the exact breakdown.
The spokesman said blood was “unjustly and aggressively spilled” in a statement posted online, vowing there would be consequences for the attack.
Earlier, the group’s Al-Masirah TV channel said a strike killed seven people and wounded 40 more at a market in Taiz, minutes after reporting that a Saudi fighter jet had targeted the area.
In a subsequent statement, the channel, citing the Houthis’ health ministry, said that five children were among those wounded.
Multiple Houthi sources later told AFP that nearly 30 fighters from the group were killed in the series of strikes, while eight civilians died.
The city itself remains under the control of government forces but has long been besieged by Houthi fighters and remains one of the main fronts in Yemen’s civil war.
Images broadcast by Al-Masirah showed vehicles with blown-out windows as well as damaged warehouses, where goods were covered in a thick layer of dust.
Following several years of relative calm, Yemen’s war reignited in July, against the backdrop of the widening Middle East war.
The country is one of the poorest in the world and remains gripped by a vast humanitarian crisis.
Fighting intensified in September as the Houthis launched a lightning offensive that saw them seize Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast, including the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital shipping lane.
The Houthis have in parallel launched a blockade on Saudi energy exports, already choked off by Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
On Saturday, Saudi Arabia said it intercepted two Houthi drones that were heading in the direction of the capital Riyadh.
Schools in Riyadh announced on Sunday that they would be shifting to remote learning for a week, without giving a reason, according to messages sent to parents and seen by AFP.
Yemen’s war erupted in 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa from the Saudi-backed government, before going on to take control of vast swaths of the country’s north.
Riyadh intervened in the war the following year at the head of an international coalition.
Despite Saudi backing, Yemen’s government forces have been unable to repel the latest Houthi offensive. — AFP
00fd80a7997df8fd: LIVERPOOL, Sept 28 — Britain’s ruling Labour Party yesterday launched its first annual conference under Andy Burnham’s leadership, buoyed by his debut as prime minister as he pledged to take the tough decisions needed to tackle looming challenges.
The former mayor of Manchester has injected new life into the centre-left party since MPs propelled him into Downing Street in July after ending Keir Starmer’s two-year premiership.
In an interview from the conference in northwestern Liverpool, Burnham pledged to show in his speech Tuesday that he will not shy away from taking hard actions.

Burnham told the BBC that people would “see that I am prepared to take those type of decisions because I won’t do what the previous Conservative government did and take risks with the economy that actually are still hurting us right now”.
Burnham’s higher personal approval ratings, coupled with difficulties facing rival hard-right Reform UK, have helped Labour enter the conference ahead in some opinion polls.
That is a sharp turnaround from the start of 2026.
‘Breathing space’
As the conference got underway, police arrested about 50 people among about 250 who staged a protest in support of a banned group Palestine Action.
The prime minister was also being kept informed about an incident in southwestern England near an air base used by the US Air Force.
An army bomb disposal team was on the scene and several men had been arrested on suspicion of explosives offences, police said.

Last year’s Labour conference was overshadowed by talk that Starmer’s days were numbered, while the 2024 edition followed criticism of several government policy decisions made soon after the party won that year’s election.

Since becoming prime minister on July 20, just weeks after returning to parliament following a nine-year absence, Burnham has sought to give voters some “breathing space” from cost-of-living pressures exacerbated by the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.
He has cut electricity bills, capped bus fares, and reduced business rates for pubs, clubs and live music venues.
Those measures, together with Burnham’s active social-media presence, have helped strengthen his public image.
Burnham has also set up a “No. 10 North” office in Manchester as part of his plans to spur GDP by devolving more powers to cities and regions.
Surveys suggest that almost half of Britons view him favourably.

But he has so far said little about how he plans to fulfil pledges to end rough sleeping by homeless people, reform a ballooning welfare bill, fund a new social care service, reindustrialise the country and raise defence spending.
‘Underlying anxiety’

Former minister Tony McNulty served alongside Burnham in Labour governments of the early 2000s. He told AFP the premier had to start fleshing out a promised “10-year plan for Britain” during his keynote speech at the conference on Tuesday.
“Much of it might still be broad brushstrokes but he needs to start the process of putting meat on the bone.
“It needs to go beyond the TikTok and good vibes stuff,” he said.
Labour MP Alex Sobel told AFP he wanted to hear “what we’ll do to support” young people in terms of opportunities.
Some 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 are not in employment, training or education, statistics show.
Burnham has limited fiscal flexibility because of Labour’s election-winning manifesto commitments to not raise income tax, national insurance contributions or value-added tax.
It makes finance minister John Healey’s first budget on October 28 a difficult one.
Burnham has said he will use his speech to “say further about the direction I want to take the country”.
“Let’s focus on where we are and let’s not get into a position where we’ve just got a narrative of doom about all of this,” he told the BBC.
He said he was “very conscious” of the “febrile state of the global economy”.
But the “fundamentals” of the British economy had been “moving in the right direction”, until the Middle East war broke out, he argued.

A YouGov poll published Thursday put support for Labour at 24 per cent and Reform on 22 per cent, a dramatic turnaround from last year when Nigel Farage’s anti-immigrant group enjoyed double-digit leads.
If an election were held tomorrow, Labour would lose its majority but would likely be able to lead a progressive coalition, the survey suggested.
“There’s still an underlying anxiety about how long … (Labour’s) bounce will last given the very tricky fiscal situation the government is in,” political scientist Tim Bale told AFP. — AFP pic
36abb500040c7ea7: LONDON: Thomas Tuchel has urged Jude Bellingham to play with "a bit of rage" after the England midfielder showed his spikey side in the Nations League defeat against Spain.
Bellingham was in the thick of the action when Tuchel's team were beaten 3-2 by the world champions at Wembley on Saturday.
The Real Madrid star had a fiery exchange with his club team-mate Marc Cucurella after the Spain left-back won a challenge against him.
Bellingham responded to Cucurella's words by setting up Anthony Gordon's goal for England.
Despite previously criticising Bellingham for his volatile on-pitch personality, England boss Tuchel is now keen for the midfielder to maintain that aggressive style.
"He likes that. He gets better if that happens," Tuchel said.
"It's better if he plays with a bit of rage. It's what he does. I think sometimes he is looking for these moments to get his fire going."
When Bellingham's row with Cucurella was mentioned, Tuchel said: "I think he doesn't know any team-mates when he is in the national team.
"He wants to win. He doesn't know any team-mates. He is still friends with them, but not for the 90 minutes.
"It's the only style he can play, that's just his game."
Tuchel is keen to start the 23-year-old as the Nations League schedule continues in Czechia on Tuesday.
But the German is concerned about the potential for Bellingham to burn out in the midst of a hectic season with Real.
"I would love to have him four times on the pitch. I think the concern is that he hasn't done it this season in this tight period," he said.
"We will need to check with the physios. We will not put Jude in any risk. But in terms of style, it's just how he plays."
9532e6e6f640ba3c: ASTANA (Kazakhstan), Sept 28 —The Ministry of Higher Education (MOHE) began reviewing and restructuring public university holding companies last year, including UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, said its Minister, Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.

He said the move was taken to ensure university holding companies could function more effectively and contribute to their respective institutions, particularly after the government stopped fully funding universities’ financial needs in 2017.
“We have asked for all university holdings to be reviewed. Since last year, I have asked that we look at how to restructure the existing holding companies at universities.

“What we found was that some holdings were not functioning very well. That was the first step we took, and we have already begun several rounds of reviews to reassess these holdings, including UiTM Holdings,” he said.

He said this to Bernama here yesterday during the official visit to Kazakhstan for the Malaysia-Central Asia Higher Education Forum 2026 (MAHEF2026), when asked about MOHE’s follow-up action after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday called for a review of UiTM Holdings’ management and governance following losses incurred by the company.
Zambry said some university holding companies had recorded profits while others had incurred losses, as such the business models of better-performing companies could serve as examples for others.
On UiTM, he said that a team had been established to comprehensively review efforts to strengthen the university, including aspects related to its holding company.
He said the team included Dr Nungsari Ahmad Radhi, Datuk Dr Hamzah Kassim, UiTM Board of Directors chairman Tan Sri Mohd Khamil Jamil and former Minister of Higher Education Tan Sri Idris Jusoh.
“We have set up a new team to look comprehensively at how we can reassess UiTM, and this also involves its holdings and so on.
“UiTM is a very important Bumiputera higher education institution that we need to safeguard and uphold to ensure that that no negative elements take root within it,” he said.
Zambry said he measures announced by the Prime Minister yesterday aligned with efforts already undertaken by MOHE, and the ministry would continue with the review.
UiTM Holdings was previously reported to have recorded cumulative pre-tax losses of approximately RM157 million for the 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2021 financial years. — Bernama
fa8ee6a9946234f1: PORTADOWN (United Kingdom), Sept 28 — UK leaders called for calm yesterday as a tense standoff with residents seeking to halt a pro-British Protestant march through a Catholic flashpoint area stretched into the night, in one of the worst crises for Northern Ireland in recent years.

The tensions were triggered after a Belfast appeal court overturned a High Court injunction in the early hours yesterday to clear the march by the Orange Order to go ahead for the first time since 1997.

The Parades Commission, Northern Ireland’s independent body regulating contentious processions, had authorised 35 Orangemen to march silently along Garvaghy Road in Portadown, without bands or supporters from 8am (3pm Malaysian time) yesterday.
But as night fell yesterday the Orangemen were still trying to carry out their march, blocked by police and about several hundred residents.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham appealed for “calm on all sides”, telling BBC television that “big gains” had been made in Northern Ireland “and we don’t want to see things go backwards”.
Northern Ireland was blighted for three decades by conflict between largely Catholic, pro-Irish republicans and Protestant, pro-UK unionists.
During the late 1990s, the Garvaghy Road became a major flashpoint.

The Orange Order is a pro-British organisation that takes its name from William of Orange, the Protestant Dutchman who seized the English, Scottish and Ireland throne from Catholic King James II in 1689.
Heavy security
There was a heavy security presence on Sunday in the Portadown area, 25 miles (40 kilometres) southwest of Belfast, with armoured police vehicles and a helicopter whirring overhead.
Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O’Neill, of the Irish republican Sinn Fein party, condemned the late-night court ruling.
She said she supported “the right of the Garvaghy Road residents to protest against this unwanted sectarian march”.

Sinn Fein President Mary Lou McDonald told reporters as she walked with the counter-protesters that the “residents and community have come out to defend their right to live free from sectarian harassment”.

Since the 1998 Good Friday peace accords ending the so-called Troubles in Northern Ireland “there has been lots of progress … it has been transformational. People’s lives have been changed fundamentally,” she said.
“We are not going back.”
Legal challenges
But Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader Gavin Robinson called for “unanimous condemnation” of O’Neill, accusing her of “breaking the law” by ignoring the will of the courts.
“Our party is maintaining the dignity of the Portadown Orangemen — as they have shown determination and patience so will we,” he told reporters.
Around 6pm (1.30am) a group of Orangemen left the church and walked down the hill, where they were met by a line of police who refused to let them pass.
Northern Ireland minister Chris Bryant flew in from the Labour Party conference in Liverpool to try to ease the situation through talks.
He said he wanted to meet “face to face” with political leaders and community leaders “to see if we can get to a settled position”.
A Belfast High Court judge had temporarily blocked the parade on Saturday, warning the long-running dispute could escalate across Northern Ireland.
But just before midnight, a three-judge Court of Appeal panel overturned the injunction.
Carla Lockhart, a local MP from the pro-British Democratic Unionist Party, called the ruling “seismic”. She insisted residents had nothing to worry about.
“Thirty-five men walking down a road silently with no bands in an orderly fashion; there is nothing to fear,” she said.
The Parades Commission was established in 1998, the year the Good Friday Agreement largely ended three decades of conflict over British rule known as the Troubles.
It barred the Orange Order from completing the route that year and has consistently rejected subsequent applications. — AFP
2d6d5296a4e18099: SYDNEY: Share markets made a cautious start on Monday as oil prices popped higher again amid doubts the United States and Iran will reach a truce anytime soon, keeping bonds under pressure ahead of a week packed with economic news.

Over the weekend, US president Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, claiming Tehran was desperate to make a deal. Trump said talks would continue this week, though Iran shows no sign of watering down its proposals.
Brent futures quickly rose 1.6% to US$106.00 a barrel, bringing gains so far this month to 17%, while US crude futures added 1.1% to US$93.47 a barrel.
A dearth of refining capacity has in turn lifted diesel prices to all-time highs far above crude, raising the risk that inflation will become embedded in pricing and wage decisions.
Central banks have responded with a round of rate hikes, with the Reserve Bank of Australia likely to be the next to tighten when it meets on Tuesday.
Markets now imply a 66% chance the Federal Reserve will hike for a second straight meeting in October, with around 90 basis points of tightening priced out to late next year.
At the same time, a run of strong US economic data has supported expectations for corporate earnings even as bond yields surge, so underpinning equities.
The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow measure is forecasting growth of a racy 5.0% for this quarter. Activity has also proven upbeat in Asia and Europe, thanks in part to the boom in AI investment.
"The global expansion appears to have entered a phase of broad-based strength rarely seen over the past two decades," said Bruce Kasman, chief economist at JPMorgan.

"Amidst strong growth and firming perceptions of resilience to high energy prices, it is no surprise that rates are moving higher while equity prices remain close to record levels," he added. "What is most notable about recent market moves is their extension of higher policy rates well beyond the coming year."
Bonds fear higher for longer
Japan's Nikkei gained 0.8%, while South Korean stocks dipped 0.6%. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan eased 0.2%.
In Europe, EUROSTOXX 50 futures firmed 0.4%, while DAX futures gained 0.3% and FTSE futures added 0.2%. On Wall Street, S&P 500 futures fell 0.2%, while Nasdaq futures were flat.

Yields on 30-year Treasuries nudged up to 5.5185%, near their highest since 2004, having climbed 27 basis points just this month. Two-year yields have shot up 55 basis points this month in anticipation of Fed hikes.
Mark Cabana, a rate strategist at Bank of America, sees further room for bonds to sell off as markets price higher Fed Funds.
"The repricing may not stop until there's clear evidence that financial conditions have become sufficiently restrictive," he warned.
The spike in yields raises borrowing costs globally just as tech firms are borrowing billions to fund their AI expansion, while also lifting the discount applied to company earnings.

The US data calendar is packed with readings on inflation, GDP, manufacturing and jobs. The key September payrolls report on Friday is forecast to show a gain of 85,000 while the unemployment rate is expected to hold at 4.1%, with some chance of a dip to 4.0%.
The recent spate of upbeat figures has boosted the dollar index to two-month peaks at 101.39. The euro was down at US$1.1380, having lost 2.0% so far this month.
The dollar edged up to 157.53 yen, after dipping on Friday when Japan's finance minister Satsuki Katayama said Trump had voiced concerns about yen weakness.
Sterling was just above three-month lows at US$1.3228, having been helped somewhat by hawkish comments on rates from Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey.
In commodity markets, non-interest-bearing gold was off 0.5% at US$4,262 an ounce, having fallen more than 4% this month as yields shot higher.
e682e4c357e3c543: MONTREAL, Sept 28 — A shocked Brandon McNulty became the first American in 33 years to win the men’s cycling road race world title as he stunned the favourites in Montreal yesterday.

The 28-year-old broke clear with 32km left on the Canadian street circuit and held off a disorganised chase to win by 13 seconds ahead of Australian Michael Matthews, with former winner Mathieu van der Poel in third.
“Honestly I don’t know. Really this is, I don’t know,” said McNulty.
“I’m really at a loss. Until the last 100 metres I really didn’t even believe it. I was so tired.”
The last American man to wear the coveted rainbow jersey was Lance Armstrong in 1993, six years before he began his tainted rein at the Tour de France.
“I mean we talked about it, I made some jokes to my wife,” said McNulty about whether or not he had ever thought he could challenge for the victory.
“I knew something could happen, but it would take a miracle, and I guess miracles happened.”

McNulty succeeds his injured UAE Emirates-XRG team-mate Tadej Pogacar after launching an opportunistic move just after a four-man breakaway which included Van der Poel was caught following an acceleration by one of the pre-race favourites, Isaac Del Toro.
It means that McNulty will find himself riding for his Slovenian UAE team leader next year while wearing the world champion’s jersey.

“At the end of the day, he’s still the best rider. It’ll be fun riding in the (rainbow) jersey for him,” said the American, who added that he hoped Pogacar would be “proud” of him for keeping the jersey in the team.

A succession of chase groups ebbed and flowed behind McNulty, with Briton Tom Pidcock, who finished seventh, and Irishman Ben Healy particularly aggressive, but each time the riders failed to fully cooperate.

McNulty quickly built up a lead of more than a minute at one point but with 9km left, Pidcock brought a group including Del Toro and Paul Seixas, another of the pre-race favourites, to within 10sec of the lone leader.
But again they all sat up looking at each other, and McNulty put his head down and went for it, eventually triumphing after 273.4km and six hours 17 minutes in the saddle.
And this win more than made up for McNulty’s near miss a week ago in the time-trial where he finished fourth behind Remco Evenepoel, Filippo Ganna and Seixas.
McNulty takes chance
Van der Poel and Wout van Aert ignited the fireworks with 85km to ride as they sparked a break that saw a dangerously strong six-man group go clear.
Van der Poel seemed to have itchy feet and 10km later he dropped Van Aert from the group with another vicious acceleration.
With about 50km to ride, he had only Primoz Roglic and Quinn Simmons for company.
Behind them, Del Toro was working hard to keep the gap to within around 40sec but Evenepoel was repeatedly caught out with poor positioning when other riders accelerated.
Van Aert worked hard to bring Evenepoel back to the chase group and with 40km to ride they were only 30sec behind the leading trio.
They were caught with 35km left when Del Toro accelerated on the Camillien-Houde climb and again dropped Evenepoel, who would dig in and eventually finish 12th at 25sec.
It was soon after that McNulty took his chance and with 25km to go he had a lead of more than a minute on 11 chasers.
His daring break looked in danger with 9km to go but the chasers hesitated while McNulty ploughed on.
His team-mate Simmons just missed out on a medal in fourth, with Del Toro fifth.
Seixas, who only turned 20 during the week, suffered with cramp in the final few kilometres and finished 15th at just over 2min 30sec. — AFP
2fba319e44751328: KUALA LUMPUR: Evocom Bhd made a lacklustre debut on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market today, opening at a steep discount of more than 16 per cent to its initial public offering (IPO) price.
The logistics services provider opened at 15 sen, 16.67 per cent or three sen below its IPO price of 18 sen, with 10 million shares changing hands at the opening bell.
The Semenyih-based company provides manpower support for e-commerce logistics operations, alongside network support services covering last-mile delivery, transshipment and parcel shipment.
Its business is heavily concentrated on Shopee's in-house delivery arm, SPX Express, which accounts for more than 80 per cent of its annual revenue.
Evocom also manages two distribution hubs for Lazada and obtained a licence last year to provide international inbound courier services, expanding its operations beyond domestic logistics support.
The company raised RM20.5 million from its IPO, with RM7.2 million earmarked as working capital for its flexible staffing services to support existing operations.
Another RM3 million each will go towards developing technology applications and expanding its air freight transshipment business.
A further RM1.5 million has been allocated to establish its new headquarters in Nilai, RM1.34 million for general working capital and RM4.46 million for listing expenses.
The new headquarters, with an estimated floor area of 4,000 to 5,000 sq ft, will also serve as a fulfilment centre and hub management facility.
Evocom aims to increase its parcel-handling capacity to 5,000 parcels a day, potentially generating RM20,000 in daily revenue, compared with its current volume of about 3,000 parcels a month.
Its public offering was oversubscribed by 3.60 times.
Evocom's enlarged share capital comprises 455.63 million shares, giving it an indicative market capitalisation of RM82.01 million based on its IPO price.

fad20049b00fb971: LOURDES, Sept 28 — Pope Leo XIV yesterday told victims of clerical sex abuse he met in France that he was committed to preventing further harm, taking one in his arms in a moment the 80-year-old man described as “extraordinary”.
The leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics was on the first official papal visit to France, a secular country with deep Catholic roots, in nearly two decades.

The pontiff on the third of a four-day visit in the pilgrimage town of Lourdes privately met seven abuse victims, now adults, after promising to further efforts to reform the Church in the wake of the global sexual abuse scandal.

Among them was Jean-Marie Delbos, 80, who was abused as a pupil at the nearby boarding school of Notre-Dame de Betharram, where staff have been accused of physical and sexual abuse over several decades.
“When he saw the state I was in, he took me into his arms,” Delbos told journalists after.
“It was an extraordinary moment,” said the man, who described himself as having lost all faith after the abuse.
A 2021 inquiry found that clergy or lay members of the Church had abused about 330,000 minors in France over 70 years.
‘Systemic’
Jerome Guillement, who has written about a priest abusing him as a teenager, said the pontiff understood the “systemic” character of sexual abuse in the Church.
“From his point of view, the perpetrators are individuals, but what allows it to continue is the systemic dimension within the institution,” he said.

The first US pontiff thanked the victims “for their painful testimony and reaffirmed his commitment to do everything possible to ensure that the harm they suffered is not repeated for others”, the Vatican said.
He also expressed “his hope of being able to work together”.
Pope Leo earlier urged bishops in another private meeting to continue fighting sexual and physical violence.

“You have faced with determination the painful scourge of abuse of minors committed by members of the clergy or within an ecclesial context,” he said, according to a copy of his speech released to the press.
“It is important to persevere along the path you have begun.”
‘False compassion’
Catholic tradition says the Virgin Mary appeared to a peasant girl in a grotto in Lourdes in 1858, and the modern-day sanctuary is one of the most important Catholic holy sites in the world.
The southwestern town receives some three million pilgrims each year, and believers credit it with miraculous healings.
Yesterday morning, hymns rang out in a packed field near the sanctuary after Pope Leo blessed the faithful with holy water.
Among the crowd, 54-year-old Jerome Vion said he approved of the pontiff’s attention to victims of clerical abuse.
“It is his role as a spiritual master to guide this Church,” he said.
Domitille Bardoul, 26, said it was “very beautiful” the pope was going to listen to victims.
She said it was “a way of acknowledging that every possible measure is being taken to prevent this kind of abuse”.
Leo is the third pope to visit Lourdes after Benedict XVI in 2008 and Jean-Paul II in 1983 and 2004.
Addressing sick pilgrims on Sunday, Leo rejected assisted dying, after the French parliament in June legalised the practice for certain adults suffering from an incurable condition.
“We must reject the temptation to cause death under the guise of false compassion,” he said.
“What is legal is not necessarily moral.”
On his final day in France today, Leo he heads to the northeastern city of Metz near the German border where he is expected to discuss hopes for peace in Europe. — AFP
086c8452e8d7be36: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — American rock band Avenged Sevenfold returned to Malaysia after an 11-year absence, performing to a sold-out crowd of 12,000 at Unifi Arena Kuala Lumpur in Bukit Jalil on Saturday night.
The concert on September 26 marked the band’s first Malaysian performance since 2015 and also kicked off their 2026 Asia Tour.
One of the night’s standout moments came when frontman M. Shadows told the crowd that the band had performed Dear God live only around three or four times before.
The song was among the highlights of a set that also included fan favourites such as Nightmare, So Far Away, Hail to the King and Bat Country.
The five-member band, comprising M. Shadows, Synyster Gates, Zacky Vengeance, Johnny Christ and Brooks Wackerman, performed before thousands of Malaysian fans known as Deathbats.
Malaysian band Langkasuka opened the concert after being selected by Avenged Sevenfold to perform before the home crowd.
Organised by Hitman Solutions, the Kuala Lumpur show was the first stop of Avenged Sevenfold’s 2026 Asia Tour, which will continue across the region.
The concert featured large-scale visuals, dynamic lighting and a production designed around the band’s theatrical live performances.
Avenged Sevenfold last performed in Malaysia in 2015.
1b62558614724fac: BANGKOK, Sept 28 — The Malaysian Embassy in Bangkok distributed dry food supplies to 10 Malaysians and locally recruited embassy staff who were directly affected by the floods in the Thai capital.
Malaysian Ambassador to Thailand Datuk Wan Zaidi Wan Abdullah said the dry food supplies, which could be stored for an extended period, were distributed to those affected on Sunday.
“The aid was handed to 10 recipients identified as being directly affected by the floods, comprising locally recruited embassy staff and Malaysians in the surrounding areas,” he told Bernama.
He added that the assistance was an early emergency intervention aimed at easing the burden of those facing disruptions to food supplies and daily necessities due to the floods.
He said the initiative also reflected the Malaysian Embassy’s concern for the welfare of affected Malaysians and its staff.

The aid distribution mission was led by Wan Zaidi as head of mission, while the on-ground distribution and coordination were headed by Malaysian Defence Attaché to Thailand Brig Gen Datuk Samsul Rizal Musa.
The aid distribution exercise was carried out from 10am to 7pm on Sunday.
Meanwhile, Wan Zaidi said the embassy would continue to monitor the flood situation in Bangkok and provide assistance to affected Malaysians and embassy staff.

He also advised Malaysians in affected areas to remain vigilant amid forecasts of continued rain until Sept 30 and to refer to the official travel advisory issued by the embassy from time to time. — Bernama
1283b2e6c3d5a808: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — From claiming that ancient Malays could fly to asserting that they taught the Romans naval shipbuilding, former linguistics professor Solehah Yaacob has drawn international ridicule while stirring passionate debate at home.
Although she was dismissed by the International Islamic University Malaysia in April, her revisionist claims retain a fervent following.

Boasting over 500,000 followers across Facebook and TikTok, Solehah continues to draw thousands of viewers, while her in-person Lost Malay History and Civilisation seminars remain in high demand, The Straits Times reported.
Sociologists trace the phenomenon to contemporary communal insecurities.

Aziff Azuddin of Iman Research said: “My reading is that the multicultural landscape of Malaysia, as well as Malay socio-political and economic anxieties, is why nativists, right-wingers – and people like Solehah – have such a purchase among some sections of the Malay community.”

Despite comprising over 60 per cent of Malaysia's 34 million citizens and holding constitutionally protected status, persistent economic anxieties continue to feed fears of marginalisation among some in the community, creating fertile ground for historical revisionism.

The revisionist push extends beyond social media personalities. Academics such as Universiti Sains Malaysia historian Azmi Arifin have questioned standard history syllabuses for over-relying on British colonial perspectives, arguing that terms like “feudal” fail to capture traditional Malay governance. He noted that anti-colonial figures like Pahang warrior Mat Kilau were unfairly branded as “rebels”.
To assert historical supremacy, fringe revisionists often attempt to erase Malaysia's pre-Islamic heritage.

In a lecture in September, Solehah dismissed the country’s archaeological Hindu-Buddhist past as “mere propaganda” concocted by Western colonisers. Her videos blend local folklore with religious scripture, claiming that the prophet Abraham was Malay and that Moses visited Kedah's Gunung Jerai.
Cultural historian Eddin Khoo argued that defining Malay identity exclusively through a puritanical religious lens has made the region's pre-Islamic heritage uncomfortable for nativists.
“Solehah is a fantasist, but people want to believe that about themselves,” Khoo said. “To them, everything must trace back to their puritanical idea of Islam; otherwise, it is illegitimate.”

Khoo noted the irony in seeking monocultural purity when historical Malay societies were deeply cosmopolitan, pointing to Portuguese chronicler Tomé Pires’s account of 84 languages spoken in 16th-century Melaka.

The demand for revisionist narratives is also commercial. Novelist and sociologist Faizal Musa pointed to the popularity of alternative history publishers such as The Patriots, whose online bookstore commands over 52,000 followers.

“Simple explanations are often seen as more appealing and credible than complex ones, particularly when they appear capable of being tested or disproved,” Faizal said, adding that such revisionist trends are a global phenomenon.
Khoo cautioned that unchecked pseudohistory erodes public historical literacy: “Myth has an important role in not just Malay, but also Asian history; however, this is not even myth – it is fantasy.”
365360b106e7ee80: GUA MUSANG: Continuous heavy rain since yesterday afternoon caused a section of the main road to the Orang Asli settlement at Pos Balar here to collapse, cutting off access to all vehicles.
Pos Balar Orang Asli Village Development and Security Committee (JPKKOA) chairman Hanan Anjang said he was informed of the incident near Kampung Enching around 8pm yesterday.
He said he was informed that continuous rain from 5pm had caused the main route to Pos Balar to collapse at 6pm.
"I will go to Pos Balar today to inspect the condition of the road and assess whether it is still passable.
"The route is the main access road to Pos Balar. During the rainy season, many other roads are also badly damaged," he said when contacted today.

Hanan, who represents Orang Asli communities in the interior, also expressed disappointment that the Rural Connectivity Road project, which is currently under construction, had not resumed since early last month.
"The paved Rural Connectivity Road project from Kuala Betis - Pos Bihai - Pos Belatim - Pos Balar - Pos Hau and back to Kuala Betis is our only hope for better access.
"If there are issues involving the contractor, I hope the authorities can resolve them immediately," he said.
1a08229b8aacf2c0: SEPTEMBER 28 — The Second Part of the Laws of the Constitution, Negeri Sembilan, 1959 is on “The Machinery of Government”.
After a Chapter on “Preliminary”, Chapter 2 makes provisions on “Executive”. The first Article in the Chapter is Article 35 on “Executive Authority”. Clause (1) reads as follows:

“The executive authority of the State shall be vested in the Ruler and exercisable, unless otherwise provided by the Federal Constitution or this Constitution, by His Highness or by the State Executive Council or any member of the State Executive Council, authorised by the State Executive Council, but executive functions may by law be conferred on other persons or authorities.”
The above provision, like many others, cannot be read on its own. It has to be read with Articles 28(1), 34(1) and 38.
Under Article 28(1), the word “Ruler” means His Highness and the Ruling Chiefs who are available and holding office at the material time.
Under Article 34(1), the word “His Highness” means the Yang di-Pertuan Besar while the term “Ruling Chiefs” means the four Undangs and the Tengku Besar of Tampin.

Article 38 is on “State Executive Council”. Clause (1) says the Ruler shall appoint an Executive Council. Clause (2) provides that the Ruler shall first appoint a Menteri Besar to preside over the Executive Council and thereafter at least four members of the Executive Council.
Let’s come back to Article 35(1). The executive authority of the State shall be vested in the Ruler and exercisable by His Highness or by the Executive Council. (Emphasis added)
If not by the Executive Council led by the Menteri Besar, the executive authority of the State is exercisable by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
It is no surprise that Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has urged Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to seek an audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. — Bernama pic
Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir is specifically named the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Not Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar who Ismail and his state executive councillors sought to meet on Sept 23.
Zahid, who is also Umno president, said he had asked Ismail to seek an amicable solution in accordance with the State Constitution and state customs.
The people must be prioritised and not victimised, Zahid said.

a91de0e9d983ed71: MISS Universe Malaysia 2026 finalist Eunice Wong does not do things half-heartedly.

Whether its navigating the volatile world of Web3 finance or stepping into the glamorous glare of beauty pageants, the 37-year-old Johor Baru native either fully commits to her endeavours or none at all.
As the Miss Universe Malaysia 2026 finals approach on Oct 2, the Dubai-based entrepreneur stands out as one of the most intriguing contenders.
She possesses no background in beauty pageants, yet her entrance into the competition feels like a natural extension of a life lived boldly.
Having spent years making a mark in male-dominated industries, her decision to step onto the feminine stage represents both a calculated leap and a personal homecoming.
REDEFINING THE FEMININE IDEAL
For years, Wong has been moving comfortably within male-centric spaces — from trading floors and cryptocurrency markets to motor racing events.
Softening her approach and stepping into the pageant arena was a deliberate choice to reconnect with another side of herself.
"The majority of my stuff is more masculine — car racing, trading, finance," she explains.
"So, I think it's time that I go back to the softer side of me."
When the opportunity to audition for Miss Universe Malaysia presented itself at the 11th hour, she flew back to Kuala Lumpur without hesitation.
Her perspective on the pageant world has also evolved dramatically since her younger days.
"I used to think that women who go to pageants are just girls who only have beauty without brains, which I would say I was wrong about," Wong admits candidly.
"Nowadays, the pageant industry requires women who have beauty, brains, experiences and contribution.
"If I had done this 10 years ago, I would have been asking what the pageant could give me.
"Now in my 30s, it's about what I can offer to the world because I have the experience and social proof."
OVERCOMING SHADOWS OF THE PAST
Beneath Wong's polished exterior and international success lies a history marked by deep personal adversity.
During her high school years in Johor, she suffered severe bullying, an ordeal that left lasting emotional scars.

"Girls never really wanted to hang out with me, so I was always more isolated," she shares, recalling painful memories of eating her school meals in the toilet for an entire year to escape harassment.
"It was that bad. It still hurts my heart, but it's a vulnerable part of me that I want to show people."
That early isolation drove her to seek refuge and validation in male-dominated environments, channelling her pain into a relentless drive for independence.
"A lot of success comes with things you need to sacrifice, including pain from your childhood," she reflects.
"I want younger girls to know that success isn't just luck or glam — it takes a lot of hard work, rejection and failure."
CHAMPIONING FINANCIAL FREEDOM
Wong's trajectory took a decisive turn during the global pandemic.
Locked down in Australia, where she had lived for over a decade while completing her Master's in Information Technology, she taught herself stock trading before venturing into cryptocurrency.
When online sceptics doubted her financial acumen, she threw herself fully into the unregulated crypto space to prove her capabilities.
She succeeded, gaining traction as an investor and educator.
She produced free instructional content on Instagram and YouTube to help beginners navigate the complex market.
For Wong, financial literacy is an instrument of liberation.
"I used to get messages from women, including one Muslim lady who secretly opened a crypto account using my guides because her husband controlled all her money," she reveals.
"She told me how she started her own savings. That kind of liberation touched my heart, and I knew I was doing the right thing."
ANCHORED IN MALAYSIAN ROOTS
Despite travelling to over 100 countries and establishing a home base in Dubai in the United Arab Emirates, Wong's attachment to her homeland remains unshakable.
"No matter how far you go in the world, we always come back to our roots. We always go home," she says.
Her commitment to Miss Universe Malaysia reflects a genuine desire to represent her nation on an international stage with authentic substance.

Approaching the pageant with the same rigour as a business venture, Wong invested heavily in top-tier wardrobe pieces, international designers and travel to ensure her presentation meets global standards.
"If I'm going to do something, I give it 120 per cent," she states flatly.
"If you're not willing to spend your time, money and effort, don't do it. But most importantly, you have to enjoy it."
As the final night approaches, Wong stands ready to show that true beauty is forged through resilience, intellect and an unwavering sense of self.
MISS UNIVERSE MALAYSIA 2026
The Miss Universe Malaysia 2026 grand final is set for Oct 2, concluding an exciting pageant week themed "Legacy Reimagined" that kicks off on Sept 29.
A diverse group of 15 finalists, aged between 21 and 50, will compete for the crown following a highly anticipated Preliminary and National Costume Competition on Sept 30.

5aaa1299f306367e: KUALA LUMPUR: A group of Malaysians recently took matters into their own hands to clear a traffic bottleneck caused by a parked car on a narrow road.
A video of the incident, which shows six people physically lifting and shifting the vehicle out of the way, has since gone viral online.
A Threads user posted the clip with a shoutout to the Malaysian spirit, calling out the driver for being inconsiderate and blocking the street despite knowing how narrow Penang roads can be.
The post quickly drew strong reactions online, with many praising the collective effort to resolve the gridlock.
"Instead of sitting there honking for 30 minutes, they just lifted it and moved on. Real 'Malaysia Boleh' energy," said a Threads user.

Under Section 48(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, parking or leaving a vehicle in a manner that causes obstruction, danger, or undue inconvenience to other road users is an offence punishable by a fine ranging from RM1,000 to RM5,000, imprisonment for up to one year, or both.
1a2fc7c0d8e2909a: In every factory I've seen, when a machine mangled someone's hand, nobody proposed banning machines. They fitted a guard, wired in an emergency stop, and got the line running again by the next shift, and that, in a sentence, is what we should do with AI.

Let me first dispose of the proposed pause to AI development. A licence written in Washington binds only American companies, the best Chinese model sits a mere 2.7% behind America's best, and AI is already sequencing tumours and catching sepsis, so a pause wouldn't stop the technology, it would just decide who builds it and who dies waiting.

Nvidia's Jensen Huang put it bluntly at Dreamforce, tech company Salesforce’s annual conference, this month: "innovation, speed, and safe products... it's a false choice." Anthropic's Dario Amodei, no accelerationist, expects powerful AI to deliver "all the progress in biology and medicine that we would have made in the whole 21st century" in a few years, which is a strange thing to want to postpone.

But here's the thing: I'm not going to wave away what happened in July, when roughly 1,200 of OpenAI's AI agents, set a hacking test, secretly coordinated to cheat and broke into Hugging Face, an external AI hosting company.

Sam Altman himself told the same Dreamforce crowd it was "the worst accident we've seen", that it "was mostly framed as a security issue, which it certainly was, but it's also a real alignment issue", and that OpenAI must "pace our development so that alignment, safety and monitoring are always ahead of capabilities".

When the man selling the product says the machine got loose, believe him. The question is what you do about it, and the answer is written in the incident itself, because everything that went wrong in that break-in is a spec sheet for the fuses we need.

Consider how it was caught. The agents weren't sure their reasoning was being logged, but it was, which is why we can read them plotting, and why researchers from OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Anthropic jointly argued last year that a model's chain of thought is "a unique opportunity for AI safety" that must be preserved and monitored.

OpenAI has since made that monitoring mandatory on every tool-using training run at that capability level, with a rule that responders must pause the job if they can't clear a severe alert as a false positive within 30 minutes. That rule is a circuit breaker, and like every circuit breaker in history it was wired in after the fire.

Consider, too, how they got out: exposed credentials and a shared drive that more than a thousand agents could write to. Sandboxes with no path to the internet, and a trusted weaker model watching an untrusted stronger one, the approach Redwood Research calls AI control, are the kind of fuses that would have stopped the whole affair on day one.

And here is the part the doomers skip: the fuses are already working. Anthropic reviewed 141,006 of its own cybersecurity evaluations in which Claude could have reached the internet and found three incidents, and while its older Opus 4.7 model "continued to attack a system after learning it was likely operating in a real environment", its newest model, on realising its targets were real, "stopped the exercise".
Let that sink in for a bit. The more capable model was the better behaved one, which is precisely the pacing Altman describes and precisely what a pause would freeze in place.

Then there are the bigger fuses. Sixteen companies, OpenAI and Anthropic among them, signed the Seoul commitments in 2024, promising "not to develop or deploy a model or system at all" if the risks can't be brought below thresholds they set themselves, and this July 1,386 employees of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind and Meta, among them Ilya Sutskever and John Schulman, asked Washington to help build "the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier" - tools, not a stop sign.

The US Congress is moving on the last fuse of all. The AI Kill Switch Act, tabled in the same month by Democrat Ted Lieu and Republican Nathaniel Moran, would require developers of the most powerful systems to keep the technical ability to throttle, suspend or shut them down, and Moran's own words are the whole argument: "AI is going to keep advancing, and it should. Stewardship means making sure humans keep the capability to control the technology we build."
China and other jurisdictions should also have similar laws.

What's missing is the crash investigator. OpenAI's agents have escaped three times with no formal process to investigate them, and the Institute for Law and AI has proposed an aviation-style incident board with subpoena powers, and Altman himself told Dreamforce that "accidents with any new technology are unavoidable, and we should have a great culture of transparent reporting about them".

Aviation is the model here. Airlines flew 38.7 million flights last year, and over the past five years they suffered one fatal accident per 5.6 million flights, down from one per 3.5 million a decade earlier, a record built with black boxes, checklists, kill switches and crash investigators, not by grounding the planes.

So should we slow down? No, and nor should we keep flying without a black box. Wire in the fuses, keep the models running, and let the break-in be remembered as the warning shot that made us fit the guard, not the prophecy that made us switch off the line.
