67c75a501bdd3872: PETALING JAYA: Long before Jumat Lias Mansor’s truck comes to a stop, the animals already know he has arrived. At each feeding spot, stray dogs wag their tails while cats gather nearby to greet the man they have learnt to trust.
For Jumat, better known as AJ “Pyro” Lias Mansor, their welcome makes every feeding round worthwhile. “They remember and appreciate you. They cannot talk, but you can feel it,” he said.
With his muscular build, the 52-year-old looks every much the formidable mixed martial arts (MMA) fighter he once was. But beneath that tough exterior lies a gentle heart.

His sporting career has spanned several disciplines. A former Malaysian national rugby player and silat athlete, he is also a Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt with experience in wrestling and Muay Thai.
In 2013, he became the first ONE Featherweight Malaysia Tournament champion.
These days, he channels that same energy and determination into a different cause: giving Sabah’s stray dogs and cats a better life.
“It’s an everyday battle. I feed them, care for them and neuter them. Then I see news of people abusing animals or dumping their pets. It’s a neverending story," he told FMT Lifestyle.
"But if I stop, who is going to take care of them? Who is going to fight for them?"

Every day, AJ feeds more than 30 stray cats and dogs in and around Kota Kinabalu. He also rescues injured and sick animals wherever he can, and carries out trap-neuter-release-manage (TNRM) efforts to help control the stray population.
His work can take him beyond the city to Kudat and Keningau, where he similarly feed animals, carries out TNRM measures, and encourages pet owners to neuter their animals.

At home, AJ and his wife care for rescued cats and dogs with special needs. Some are affected by canine distemper, while one of their pets has lost an eye - but all have found a safe place to call home.
AJ’s love for animals began in childhood. During his years as an athlete, he would travel with cat and dog food so he could feed strays wherever he went.

When the pandemic struck and restaurants closed, he worried that many strays would lose their usual food sources. So he began going out to feed them regularly and taking injured animals to veterinary clinics.
As a Muslim, AJ has been questioned about helping dogs. His response is rooted firmly in his faith.
“Islam teaches us not to hurt any animals because they are God’s creatures,” he said, stressing that Islamic teachings also provide guidance on cleansing oneself after contact with a dog.
If a dog poses a threat, he added, the matter should be left to the relevant authorities and not taken into one's own hands.
“You cannot go and kill the dog. You might not even identify the right dog! It comes down to awareness in our community," he said.
AJ's concern for others extends beyond animals. After his ONE tournament victory, AJ donated his winnings to victims of Typhoon Haiyan in the Philippines and later volunteered in Tacloban.
Last year, he travelled to Aceh to help people and animals affected by severe flooding.

Caring for strays requires considerable sacrifice. The cost of feeding strays and looking after animals at home costs him RM4,000 to RM5,000 a month, with expenses rising further when veterinary treatment is needed.
AJ, who works as a freelance personal trainer, shoulders most of the expense himself, although friends and social media followers sometimes contribute.
The toll is physical, too: years of sport have left AJ with spinal injuries and, despite undergoing surgery, he lives with pain much of the time.
Still, he remains determined to keep showing up for the animals that depend on him.
For AJ, lasting change requires responsible pet ownership, sustained TNRM efforts, and cooperation between authorities and animal-welfare groups.
Yet there is one simple act of kindness he believes everyone can offer. “If you don’t like dogs or cats, and you don’t want to feed or rescue them, that’s fine. Just don’t hurt them."
To support AJ’s efforts, contact him on Instagram.
6fe183af6c57cf2f: Tahun ini penduduk Malaysia dianggarkan 34.4 juta orang. Daripada jumlah itu 58.4% ialah orang Melayu. Mengikut perkiraan saya yang tak pandai kira-kira itu bermakna jumlah orang Melayu ialah 20 juta kurang lebihlah. Hampir semua atau boleh kata semuanya beragama Islam.
Katalah daripada jumlah itu 15 juta orang Melayu dewasa. Daripada jumlah itu 1 juta ialah ahli PAS. Ini menurut perangkaan Setiausaha Agungnya Takiyuddin Hassan.

Give and take anggaplah dua juta orang Melayu dewasa yang bukan ahli PAS tetapi menyokong dan mengundi parti itu. Oleh itu daripada grand total 15 juta orang Melayu dewasa tolak tiga juta yakni ahli dan penyokong PAS bakinya 12 juta.

Ertinya 12 juta orang Melayu Islam dewasa ini tidak menyokong PAS. Jika diambil kira apa kata pemimpin kanan PAS Mohd Amar Abdulah mereka – all 12 million of them “tidak faham dan tidak cinta Islam”. Ramai itu. Hence the title of this article.
Baru-baru ini ketika berucap pada satu majlis ceramah di Kelantan, beliau dilapor berkata “Kalau orang tidak faham Islam, dia tidak cinta Islam. Dia tidak akan sokong PAS. Itu asas paling mudah."
Ada lagi kata beliau: "Walaupun dia boleh jadi orang Islam, dia pergi Mekah banyak kali tapi kerana dia tidak faham dan tidak cinta kepada Islam maka dia tidak akan undi PAS”.
Menurut Mohd Amar, PAS hanya akan disokong dan diundi oleh seseorang yang mencintai Islam kerana parti itu tidak hanya bergerak dalam bidang politik tetapi juga dakwah.
Memandangkan beliau ialah naib presiden PAS, Mohd Amar ada autoriti untuk bercakap bagi pihak parti. Pada hemat saya beliau equate atau menyamakan PAS itu Islam dan Islam itu PAS.

Saya akui PAS boleh dilihat sebagai badan dakwah selain politik. Sering kuliah agama yang disampaikan pemimpin PAS (bukan semua diantara mereka yang digelar guru agama) menyelit unsur politik malah membawa mesej politik dengan jelas.
Ini kata mereka kerana agama dan politik tidak boleh dipisahkan. Memisahkan menurut mereka ialah amalan atau konsep 'secularisme'. Islam sebagai ad’din tidak memisah kedua-dua.

Namun bagi saya sering, kerap dan selalu kata-kata pemimpin PAS (sama ada yang bergelar ulama, tuan guru atau tidak) pada kuliah dan ceramah serta tindakan, tingkah laku mereka boleh diibaratkan langkah the end justifies the means.

Maksudnya matlamat atau hasrat yang diingini adalah amat penting sehingga ia menghalalkan apa jua cara untuk mencapainya. Jika seseorang Muslim tolak amalan itu adakah dia tidak faham dan tidak cinta Islam?

Pada pandangan saya, politikus PAS ialah typical politicians. Bergerak dan bertindak demi political survival mereka dan parti. Adakah ini salah dan dosa? Tidak jika dilakukan berlandaskan undang-undang? Mungkin saya sendiri tidak senang dengan cara yang digunakan.
Maksudnya meskipun ada tindakan mereka yang tidak menyalahi perundangan tetapi tetap tidak disukai dan tidak dipersetujui oleh sebahagian (besar?) masyarakat Melayu Islam.

Adakah adil menuduh mereka tidak faham Islam? OK mungkin ada (macam saya) yang tidak begitu faham soal agama. Tetapi tuduh mereka tidak cinta Islam? Hanya kerana tidak undi PAS? Seriously? Tidak wajar sama sekali.

Memang ada 'gelombang hijau'. Semakin ramai orang Melayu menyokong dan mengundi PAS. Tetapi PAS khususnya Mohd Amar mesti bertanya kepada diri sendiri mengapa masih ramai juga orang Melayu beragama Islam yang tidak sokong dan undi mereka?
Saya bercakap mengenai rakyat biasa. Tanyalah mereka. Mereka tidak cinta PAS bukan tidak cinta Islam.

Oleh kerana PAS parti politik saya timbulkan pula soal politik dan orang politik. Muhyiddin Yassin, Mohamed Azmin Ali dan parti Bersatu mengadu apa yang dilakukan PAS terhadap mereka dalam Perikatan Nasional (PN) sesuatu yang tidak adil.

Betul atau tidak soal lain. PAS pun pasti ada their side of the story. Maka tidak perlu diperinci pada penulisan ini. Bagaimanapun persoalannya adakah Bersatu tidak cinta Islam? Hanya kerana sudah tidak sokong PAS? Bergaduh actually.
Begitu juga Ahmad Awang, Mohamad Sabu dan rakan rakan yang mencabar pucuk pimpinan PAS pada pemilihan parti 2015. Umum tahu mereka tewas lantas keluar parti dan lahirlah Amanah.
Adakah mereka tidak faham dan tidak cinta Islam? Atau semasa dalam PAS 'diiktiraf' (oleh PAS ) cinta Islam luar PAS tidak ?
Sebagai rakyat marhaen saya melihat apa yang dilakukan (atau tidak dlakukan) PAS di Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah dan Perlis tidak menyakin berbanding apa yang dilakukan DAP di Pulau Pinang.
Juga tidak menyenangkan malah membimbangkan saya ialah taktik tiup sentimen perkauman yang digunakan PAS (bersama Umno). Lalu saya tidak sokong dan undi PAS.
Diakui saya kerdil mengenai Islam. Tetapi bolehkah saya dituduh tidak cinta agama saya?

Apa yang diucapkan Mohd Amar kata saya amat membimbangkan. Ia boleh disamakan dengan ucapan pemimpin PAS lain mengenai undi PAS masuk syurga .Different words same meaning. Cuma beliau lebih bijak mengatur kata-kata.

Begitu juga 'Amanat Hadi'. Hadi Awang ketika beliau dikenali sebagai a firebrand up and coming leader in PAS, pada pendapat saya tidak tuduh Umno kafir. At least not directly (seperti yang didakwa Dr Mahathir Mohamad selaku presiden Umno suatu masa dulu).
Apa yang Hadi huraikan ialah sebagai orang Islam mesti amalkan A, B, C dan D. Tetapi Ummo dakwanya tidak lakukan A, B, C dan D itu. Apa maksud beliau? Faham faham sendiri.
Kita tahu apa yang terjadi akibat Amanat Hadi. Ringkasnya pada kalangan Melayu Islam terjadi sembayang dua imam, suami isteri bercerai, keluarga berpecah dan pulau memulau.
Sesungguhnya harapan kita semua pastinya ucapan Mohd Amar tidak mencetuskan itu semua Nauzubillah min zalik.
Tetapi ada saya terbaca satu komen di media sosial. Berkata seorang hamba Allah: “Kalau tidak sokong PAS tidak faham tidak cinta Islam boleh juga dikata sokong PAS tidak faham tidak cinta Islam”.
Ini juga membimbangkan jika ia pula ada traction.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
aa28d55c80d7ba65: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Blink and you probably would have driven past Restoran Hup Kee, as the restaurant sits slightly away from the road framed under a huge tree.
There’s no flashy signboard. Just a banner proclaiming its presence.
Tables and chairs in striking fire engine red line the front. Walk ahead and push the sliding glass doors to find a small dining area plastered with festive Chinese New Year posters.
The place has aged but remains clean and welcoming.
Now the third generation runs the restaurant, carrying on their grandparents’ legacy with signature dishes like the Sweet and Sour Pork (RM13).
The simple everyman dish looks very different here: instead of flat, diamond-shaped battered meat pieces, this place serves them in round shapes, making them resemble batter-covered meatballs.
The friendly proprietress told me the dish evolved from being made with pork belly to lean pork as diners made healthier choices.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
​​​​​​​Fried Prawn and Taro may not look like much, but its golden, crunchy batter coupled with bouncy prawns and thin taro sticks is hugely satisfying like fast food. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
With its round shape, it resembles lychee pork or lizhi rou, a Fuzhou dish served with a sauce and water chestnuts.

Famed Taiwanese television chef Fu Pei Mei featured the dish in her cookbook from the 1950s and 1960s, where the pork loin is cut into thick slices, scored and marinated with soy sauce and red colouring.

She prefers to roll it into a cylinder shape before deep frying the pork and combining it with a sauce that uses sugar and vinegar thickened with cornstarch. There’s no tomato ketchup like her recipe for sweet and sour pork.
The recipe has evolved; now many marinate the meat with red glutinous rice for the colour and pair it with the same sweetish, tangy sauce used in sweet and sour pork.
This version served at Hup Kee feels like a blend of both styles: it has the circular shape of lychee pork but is married to the same sauce used in classic sweet and sour pork.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

​​​​​​​Every meal should have fish and for a change from steamed fish, this place does an excellent Deep Fried Ma Yau Fish with golden edges paired with a soy sauce that is almost like syrup. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi

Typically, ketchup and vinegar weren’t used in China; haw flakes provided that refreshing acidity in the sauce. As far as I know, only one other restaurant in Kuala Lumpur upholds that tradition with haw flakes.
Hup Kee’s sauce isn’t as sharp or sweet compared to other places and its viscosity is thinner because the sauce needs to cling to the pork; otherwise, it will soften the crispy pork.
It is that lack of acidity and cloying sweetness along with the stir fried capsicum, onions and pineapple which makes it one of my favourite renditions of this classic dish.
I probably missed some other old-school items, as I only managed two dishes: Sweet and Sour Pork and Fried Prawns and Taro (RM24).
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

This version of Mui Choy Kaw Yoke will require multiple servings of rice as the pork belly and preserved mustard greens isn’t too salty and the fat is cooked to a luscious melt in the mouth texture. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
The fried prawns are covered with a golden batter coating that is shatteringly crispy, contrasting with the chewy bouncy prawn meat and the fluffy sticks of taro.
It would have been better with more taro but again with rising costs, taro is now a premium item.
On its own, it lacks much flavour so dip it in the bottled chilli sauce served on the side.
I prefer eating it plain to taste the mild sweetness from the prawn found under its crunchy layer.
Fish is of course a must for any meal and this place offers steamed fish, a much lauded assam fish served cut into pieces instead of whole, and one of my favourites, Deep Fried Ma Yau Fish (RM68).
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
​​​​​​​Refreshing, crunchy Stir Fried Paku Pakis is topped with tiny deep fried baby prawns. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
When deep-fried, the elongated threadfin fish offers a glorious contrast of crunch and tenderness, making you want to relish every fin and the head till everything is clean.
Hup Kee’s version is even more addictive as it pairs the fish with a syrup-like soy sauce and fine crispy shreds of ginger.
As I am rather salt-averse, I anointed the fish sparingly to just lightly season it rather than letting it soak up the sauce.
It takes some time but there’s a sense of satisfaction when every bone is clean of the glorious flesh.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
​​​​​​​This bowl of spinach in a broth, topped with the frilly strands of a beaten egg, tastes just like home. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
Mui Choy Kaw Yoke (RM30) comes in a super dark mahogany brown hue that scared me into thinking it must be very salty but it wasn’t.
Distinct layers of creamy fat and lean pork melt in the mouth along with the preserved mustard greens (mui choy), which isn’t salty, ensuring every bit of the sauce was wiped clean.
You can taste that the pork belly was properly pan-fried until it formed a crust before being steamed with the mui choy and sauce until it softened.
Most diners order greens as if it’s a chore but I like how each restaurant goes beyond just stir-fried vegetables with garlic.
Refresh the palate with Stir Fried Paku Pakis (RM13), brightened up with thin slices of red capsicum, tomatoes and onions to make it look appetising with its red-green colour contrast.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Every day, regulars from the neighbourhood come here to fill their stomachs with the good food. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
The surprise addition was tiny dried shrimps that gave a short burst of briny flavour when caught amidst the greens.
Siong Tong Spinach (RM18) is on every Chinese restaurant’s menu but this place puts its own spin on the dish.

Under a mound of spinach swimming in broth dotted with red goji berries, it is partially blanketed with a layer of wispy beaten fried egg peppered with cubes of salted egg white, century eggs and strips of Spam!
It’s the home-style broth that entices you to happily finish your greens without any nagging from the parents.

Last but not least, their homemade jelly for dessert is the perfect end to the heart warming meal here with its wobbly tanginess that leaves a sweet aftertaste in my mouth and a vow to return for more old school dishes.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Who needs sorbet to cleanse your palate when you get a complimentary plate of wobbly jelly (left). Hidden slightly away from the main road, you can find the restaurant by its green banner (right). — Pictures by Lee Khang Yi
Restoran Hup Kee
4A, Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah,
Kuala Lumpur.
Open daily: 11:30am to 3pm, 5pm to 10pm
*This is an independent review where the writer paid for the meal.

1f25e75c252c632e: BEIJING: Chinese electric vehicle maker NIO said on Monday it had signed a broad deal with Zhejiang Geely Holding Group on their battery-swapping and charging businesses.

Under the deal, Geely Holding Group will acquire a 30 per cent stake in NIO Power, NIO's battery-swapping and charging unit. For the purchase, Geely will contribute its 100 per cent equity in its battery-swapping subsidiary Yiyi Power, plus 640 million yuan (US$95 million) in cash.
The transaction values NIO Power at a post-money valuation of about 16 billion yuan (US$2.38 billion).
NIO will acquire a 10 per cent equity stake in Geely's smart charging subsidiary, Haohan Energy.
The two companies will co-develop unified swapping standards and vehicle models.
NIO Power aims to have 10,000 battery swap stations in operation by 2030, with annual electricity demand expected to exceed 10 billion kWh.
Geely plans to expand its network to over 22,000 charging stations with more than 100,000 connectors by the end of 2027.
0d670ea5479dc16d: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit may be poised for gains as higher oil prices and the artificial-intelligence boom provide tailwinds for the currency, strategists say.
While the ringgit has declined 1.2% in September, lagging all Asian peers, MUFG Bank expects it to strengthen to 4.03 per dollar by year-end. Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp sees it at 4.0.
The ringgit closed 0.3% higher at 4.0738 per dollar on Friday.

A renewed climb in oil prices may bolster revenues for the energy exporting country, while Malaysia’s growing role in the AI supply chain gives it exposure to rising demand for semiconductors. With the political risk premium around some state elections also fading, strategists expect the ringgit to resume its advance.

“We could see a relief rally in the ringgit toward the year-end as macro environment concerns ease,” said Jeff Ng, head of Asia macro strategy at Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp in Singapore. “Malaysia’s overall fundamentals are still positive,” given its energy and electronic exports as well as linkages to a stronger Chinese yuan, he said.

The country’s exports have surged more than 35% in each of the five months through August, boosted by shipments of electronic products including semiconductors. Export growth averaged about 6.7% in 2025. Malaysia is now one of the world’s four largest net exporters of AI-related hardware, alongside South Korea, Taiwan and Thailand, according to the International Monetary Fund.

“Malaysia’s electronics trade surplus has been able to help offset the higher oil import bill,” said Lloyd Chan, a foreign-exchange strategist at MUFG in Singapore. “We see scope for ringgit strength,” supported by attractive sovereign bond and ringgit valuations, he added.

The local currency’s real effective exchange rate is around 2% below the 20-year average, according to data from the Bank for International Settlements. Continued bond inflows may help underpin the ringgit.

Investors will be watching the S&P Malaysia manufacturing PMI print for September due Thursday for further signs of economic expansion, as the region continues to grapple with the fallout from the Middle East. Still, Malaysia may be better placed than some peers to weather higher energy costs as one of the world’s top exporters of liquefied natural gas.

“Malaysia has been on the right side of the terms-of-trade story throughout the year,” and is best-positioned to benefit from AI investment and higher energy prices, Goldman Sachs Group Inc strategists including Danny Suwanapruti wrote in a note on Sept 18. With the central bank turning slightly more hawkish, “the conditions are in place for ringgit to outperform,” they said, recommending a long ringgit/baht trade.
9a7083769f737bf6: KUANTAN, Sept 28 — An excavator operator was found drowned after the machine he was operating overturned during cleaning work at Tasik Bera, Bera yesterday.
Bera district police chief Supt Zulkiflee Nazir said his team received a report regarding the incident at around 2.10pm Sunday.
He said the deceased was Alief Daniel Haqim Abdullah, 26, while another worker who survived was Muhammad Aiman Fikri Mohd Azhar, 28.
“Based on the information received, there were two workers at the time of the incident. One managed to escape while the other was trapped in the machine,” he said in a statement yesterday.

In addition, Pahang Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (Operations) Mohd Salahuddin Isa said in a statement that the victim’s body was found trapped in the cabin of the excavator before being extricated at 4.10pm.
“The victim was unconscious when brought ashore before being pronounced dead by the health personnel who arrived at the scene,” he also said.
Zulkiflee added that the victim’s body was sent to the hospital for an autopsy. — Bernama
2e167c66a73c96fb: RAUB: An 80-year-old man was killed after his house in Kampung Kuala Dong here was destroyed by fire last night.
Retired soldier Abdul Hamid Jaafar was believed to have been trapped in the living room during the 9.55pm blaze, with his remains later recovered by firefighters. His 76-year-old wife escaped unhurt.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Mohd Razam Taja Rahim said firefighters from the Raub station arrived at the scene at 10.20pm.
"The fire was brought under control around 10.40pm. After extinguishing the fire, firefighters inspecting the premises found the victim's remains in the living room.
"Three rooms, the kitchen and roof were completely destroyed, while about 80 per cent of the house was damaged," he said in a statement today.
It is learnt that Abdul Hamid suffered severe burns due to the intense heat.
Razam said 20 firefighters from the Raub, Sungai Koyan and Lipis stations were deployed to put out the blaze, with the operation ending at 2.13am.
Meanwhile, Dong assemblyman Datuk Fadzli Mohamad Kamal said in a Facebook post that he went to the village after being informed about the fire last night.

798eedbee751cbca: ADDIS ABABA: Ethiopia's army commander on Sunday accused Eritrea and Sudan of backing armed groups fighting its troops in the north of the country.

Heavy clashes have resumed between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and the federal government since Wednesday, raising fears of a return to a 2020-2022 civil war in which an estimated 600,000 people died.
The TPLF has seized airports and launched attacks into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara, saying they were engaged in a "defensive war" against the government of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
A humanitarian source said the Afar town of Erebti, near the border with Tigray, fell to the rebels on Sunday after being pounded by heavy artillery.
The TPLF was now advancing towards the town of Afdeera, some 100 kilometres (60 miles) to the east.
The source estimated that at least 150,000 people have been displaced in Afar, but said it was impossible to give precise numbers.
Speaking on the army's YouTube channel, army chief Field Marshal Birhanu Jula said: "We are fighting forces that are organised and allied to serve the interests of external forces.
"Neither Shaebia (Eritrea) nor the TPLF can achieve anything alone, even if they are allied, unless they are backed, supported and supplied by Sudan, Egypt and other external powers," he added.
- TV station attack -
The TPLF has allied with seven armed groups around the country, and appears to repeating a strategy from the last war of pushing south through Amhara towards Addis Ababa,
Its offensive in Afar is aimed at cutting supplies from Djibouti, which provides almost all of Ethiopia's international trade cargo, including fuel.
The headquarters of Tigrai TV, seen as the key outlet for the rebel authorities in the Tigrayan capital, Mekelle, was hit by a drone on Sunday.
"We heard a loud bang from a drone strike elsewhere and we fled the building," a journalist from the station told AFP, speaking on condition of anonymity.
The channel has not commented on the incident.
Photos taken by a local journalist showed Tigrai TV building facade damaged and blackened, with numerous windows blown out by the explosion.
Another journalist said the station, which has around 400 employees, was off-air after the attack. No reports of casualties were immediately available.
The federal government in Addis Ababa said on September 21 that Tigrai TV had been suspended "indefinitely", and banned other outlets from broadcasting its reports.
- Blockade -
Communications have been limited since Friday when telecoms providers reported major disruption to phone and internet services in Tigray, making reporting on the conflict difficult.
Many in Tigray fear a repeat of a blockade imposed by the federal government during the 2020-2022 conflict when electricity, banking, and almost all aid were cut off.
United Nations chief Antonio Guterres raised the alarm on Friday, his spokesman saying Guterres was "particularly troubled by reports of the use of drones as well as incidents of harm to civilians."
The government has a significant military advantage, with a large arsenal of drones, some 500,000 troops, and support from abroad, notably the United Arab Emirates.
But the conflict could draw in neighbouring Eritrea on the side of the rebels, as it fears landlocked Ethiopia has been planning to invade and seize a direct point of access to the Red Sea.
The TPLF ruled all of Ethiopia from 1991 to 2018 before being sidelined with Abiy's rise to the prime minister's post.
That triggered a civil war marked by widespread war crimes and sexual violence.

The Pretoria Peace Agreement of 2022, brokered by African institutions and Washington, maintained an uneasy calm until last year. But it was never fully implemented, leaving around one million people unable to return to their homes.
Sporadic clashes then resumed, with the federal forces launching multiple drone strikes in Tigray in recent months and massing troops at the border.
Rights groups have accused the TPLF of a campaign of forced recruitment this year as it prepared for renewed conflict.

688983f6c835d052: WASHINGTON, Sept 28 — US President Donald Trump said yesterday that he expects talks with Iran to resume in the coming week, despite his rejection of a truce proposal put forward by Tehran.
Iranian officials brought with them to the UN General Assembly in New York a plan for a seven-day truce followed by the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz shipping channel.
Trump dismissed the plan and has mused on resuming full-scale air strikes on Iranian targets, but he told the news platform Axios that he expects negotiations to resume.
“They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make,” Trump told Axios. “It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago.”
“They overplayed their hand,” Trump said, in the interview published Sunday.
Citing sources familiar with the matter, Axios reported that indirect talks between Washington and Tehran could take place as early as Monday.
On Sunday, Iran was still standing by its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, leaving the Gulf front of the Middle East war locked in a stalemate, while fighting rages in Yemen.
‘We will not back down’

Hormuz is a key chokepoint for the world’s energy supplies and is now central to the conflict between Washington and Tehran, which was started nearly seven months ago when the US and Israel launched a wave of strikes against Iran.

Iran’s plan called for a cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East, including in Lebanon, according to Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, and a return to the conditions in an earlier ceasefire deal that fell apart.
That agreement, which collapsed during fighting over Hormuz, called for the release of frozen Iranian assets, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil and an end to the US naval blockade.

“Our conditions are clear, and any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent upon these conditions being fulfilled. We will not back down from them,” Araghchi said on Sunday, state broadcaster IRIB reported.
“We have never closed the door to diplomacy or negotiations, but at the same time, we have never backed down from our rights.”
Washington’s ambassador to the UN, Mike Waltz, accused Tehran of demanding too much in exchange for a return to the negotiating table.

“This was, I think, a pretty cynical attempt to put something on the table that they knew was unacceptable. To ask for the release of the blockade, the sanctions, international sanctions and access to billions in assets, just to talk,” he told NBC News in an interview broadcast Sunday.
“I think it’s kind of common sense that the president doesn’t have a lot of confidence this time after we just tried a few months ago.”
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards meanwhile said that they seized an American submersible drone on Sunday in the Strait of Hormuz.
It said the underwater vehicle was being used “for espionage purposes”, adding that it was “now in the hands of the force’s specialists for data recovery”.
‘Tool for pressure’
Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding in June aimed at ending the war, reopening the strait and launching talks on Iran’s nuclear programme.
But the deal broke down shortly afterwards when Iran fired on commercial ships in Hormuz that it accused of deviating from its approved route through the waterway.
Iran requires ships to obtain authorization before passage, citing security and sovereignty reasons.
Ships that refuse to comply are regularly targeted, while the United States sporadically bombs Iranian coastal areas in retaliation.
Araghchi said at the UN that Iran has conveyed to the United States, through Qatar, a concrete seven-day plan, adding: “The choice now rests with the United States.”
Hossein Mohebi, a spokesman for Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, was quoted by Tasnim news agency as saying: “We will not cease punishing the US until Iran’s seven conditions are met.”
Mohebi had told AFP in an exclusive interview on Tuesday that ending hostilities in Yemen was also among Tehran’s demands. — AFP
2f784489c27bb7b1: KOTA KINABALU: Scientific data on elephant movements along the Pan Borneo Highway has provided practical lessons on how road projects in Sabah can better account for wildlife.

Universiti Malaysia Sabah senior lecturer Dr Nurzhafarina Othman said a project studying elephant movement and habitat use before and during highway construction in Tawai Forest Reserve had identified areas where wildlife activity overlapped with the highway alignment.
"Movement data showed that the three elephants we were monitoring — one male and two females — moved out of the area during the early stages of construction.
"We also identified several areas of concentrated elephant activity that overlap with the highway alignment," said the Seratu Aatai director in a statement.
She said the monitoring project was commissioned to Seratu Aatai and Danau Girang Field Centre, with support from Yayasan Hasanah and the Finance Ministry.
Nurzhafarina was commenting following a recent workshop here involving 60 participants from government agencies, research institutions and civil society organisations.

Organised by the Institute for Development Studies (Sabah) and 10 civil society organisations under the Humans, Habitats and Highways (3H) Coalition, the workshop examined how scientific evidence and other information could be incorporated into road infrastructure planning early enough to influence alignments, designs and budgets.

She said the survey findings had provided practical information for those involved in the highway, including recommendations that guardrails should not be installed at certain locations where they could impede elephant movement, particularly that of calves.
"This is exactly why information needs to reach planners and engineers while there is still an opportunity to act on it.
Nurzhafarina said the issue went beyond individual road projects and reflected Sabah's broader development direction.
"If Sabah wants to advance a greener development agenda, we need policies and strategies that bring development and biodiversity together from the beginning.
"We cannot continue to consider biodiversity only after the alignment, design and budget have been decided," she said.

Cardiff University professor and Danau Girang Field Centre director Professor Benoit Goossens said although efforts to prevent the Tawai Forest Reserve from being affected by highway development were ultimately unsuccessful, lessons from the area could still be applied to other road projects.

Tawai Forest Reserve was among areas affected by the development of the Pan Borneo Highway, with civil society groups previously engaging with authorities in efforts to prevent the forest reserve from being affected by the project.
"It is not too late for the Kalabakan - Maliau stretch for Phase 3.

"We were informed that the alignment and budget have not yet been finalised, so there is still time to engage with planners, contractors and their consultants to explore how the road can better respect both nature and people, and this is what we hope to do," he said.

2ceee573071b3809: SINGAPORE: Crude oil exports from key Middle East producers rebounded in September to 12.8 million barrels per day, the highest since the US-Israeli war with Iran started in February, data from Kpler showed on Monday, as Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates boosted exports.

2325e891856c7819: KUALA LUMPUR: Many people associate diabetes with high blood sugar levels, medication and dietary restrictions. What fewer people realise is that long before diabetes develops, the body often gives subtle warning signs that something is wrong.

One of the most common is insulin resistance, a condition that occurs when the body's cells become less responsive to insulin, forcing the body to work harder to keep blood sugar levels under control.
According to Dr Norlaila Mustafa, a senior consultant in medicine and endocrinology, insulin resistance is particularly common among people living with obesity.
“Almost all individuals with obesity experience insulin resistance, but that does not necessarily mean they have diabetes,” she told Bernama.
“Insulin resistance is actually the early stage that may eventually lead to diabetes if left uncontrolled.”
Norlaila explained that insulin acts like a key, helping sugar move from the bloodstream into the body's cells, where it is used for energy.
When insulin resistance develops, that process becomes less effective, causing the body to produce more insulin in an attempt to compensate.

The condition usually develops gradually rather than appearing overnight. Unhealthy eating habits, physical inactivity and weight gain are among the main contributors, although stress and poor sleep can also play a significant role.
Norlaila noted that chronic stress increases levels of the hormone cortisol, which can interfere with metabolism, while insufficient sleep is closely linked to weight gain and metabolic problems.
Left unmanaged, insulin resistance can increase the risk of developing diabetes, heart disease and high blood pressure.

More concerningly, it often develops without any obvious symptoms. Still, Norlaila said there is one physical sign that is frequently overlooked: darkened patches of skin around the neck, elbows, knuckles or body folds - a condition known as acanthosis nigricans.
“Many people assume it is dirt or poor hygiene, but it is actually one of the signs of insulin resistance,” she said. “We commonly see it among individuals who are overweight.”

While obesity remains one of the strongest risk factors, Norlaila stressed that insulin resistance can also affect people who appear slim or maintain a normal weight, particularly if they have a genetic predisposition.
She also cautioned against the frequent consumption of highly processed food, as "they contain high levels of fat, and fat cells produce hormones that lead to insulin resistance".

The good news, she said, is that preventing and managing insulin resistance often begins with simple lifestyle changes. Regular physical activity, maintaining a healthy weight and making more mindful food choices can all help reduce risk.
“It does not mean you only need to eat vegetables,” Norlaila said, "but try to reduce foods high in sugar, salt and processed ingredients.”
She also encourages people to stay active through manageable forms of exercise such as brisk walking for at least 30 minutes a day.
“Above all, we must practise a healthy lifestyle through regular exercise and proper nutrition,” she added.
86f8a76202910be3: PETALING JAYA: The Negeri Sembilan royal crisis sparked in April has dragged on for nearly half a year now, with the impasse intensifying after the Aug 1 state election and now dubbed a constitutional crisis.

The crisis began after four purported undangs (chieftains) announced the alleged removal of Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, though the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) later said three of them were not undangs at the time of the proclamation.
FMT recaps the key events that transpired in Negeri Sembilan over the past six months.

April 19 At a press conference, the four purported undangs announce the alleged removal of Tuanku Muhriz as state ruler. However, they fail to disclose the grounds and evidence for his removal, which is required under the state constitution.

April 20 Then menteri besar Aminuddin Harun rejects the chieftains’ move, saying Mubarak Dohak in particular was already removed as Sungai Ujong undang for contravening customary laws. Mubarak’s removal was affirmed by the DKU, the state’s highest customary council, on April 17.

April 27 Umno withdraws support for Aminuddin for his handling of the crisis, throwing the menteri besar’s administration into limbo. Talk of a change in government fizzles out after Bersatu backs down, preventing Umno from securing a simple majority.

May 5 The four purported chieftains file an originating summons seeking a court order for the state government and DKU to release the minutes of the April 17 DKU meeting where Mubarak’s removal was affirmed.
May 7 Pakatan Harapan and Umno agree on a political ceasefire, as Aminuddin continues to lead the state government.
May 13 The DKU moves to challenge the Seremban High Court’s jurisdiction to hear the suit on the crisis, arguing that the court has no jurisdiction to hear the matter.

June 5 The state assembly is dissolved after weeks of political tension. The High Court later grants a temporary injunction preserving the status quo in Negeri Sembilan amid the customary and constitutional crises.

On the same day, Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar is purportedly proclaimed as the “new” Yang Dipertuan Besar by one of the undangs at a five-star hotel in Melaka. Former menteri besar Rais Yatim is among those present, and claims Negeri Sembilan has a new ruler.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says Tuanku Muhriz remains the recognised Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
June 9 The Negeri Sembilan palace says the purported proclamation of the “new” ruler is invalid, and strips Tunku Nadzaruddin of his hereditary Tunku Panglima Besar title.

June 23 A Conference of Rulers meeting is postponed, reportedly over the crisis in Negeri Sembilan, with the rulers preferring that the matter be resolved by the Yang Dipertuan Besar without being dragged to the courts.
June 25 Activist Badrul Hisham Shaharin, later the Negeri Sembilan Wawasan chief, claims trial to publishing seditious material related to the Negeri Sembilan royals.

July 8 The DKU obtains leave to begin contempt proceedings against six people, including the four “undangs”, for breaching the interim injunction issued on June 5. This is later temporarily stayed by the Court of Appeal.

July 17 The four “undangs” file a judicial review application seeking a court order compelling Aminuddin to sign the purported proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz. The DKU applies to intervene on Aug 10 to challenge the alleged declaration. Next case management is on Oct 7.
July 30 Tuanku Muhriz strips Rais of his state honours.

Aug 1 The DKU reveals that three of four "undangs" who attempted to depose the ruler on April 19 were not undangs at the time. It said two were already sacked while one was never officially appointed, in reaffirming Tuanku Muhriz’s status as ruler.
Later that night, the BN-PN alliance secures a two-thirds majority in the state election to form the new state government.
Aug 2 Umno’s seven-term assemblyman Ismail Lasim is sworn in as menteri besar before Tuanku Muhriz, which comes as a surprise as he was not one of the frontrunners.
Aug 6 State Umno chief Jalaluddin Alias rubbishes allegations that he aims to oust Ismail as menteri besar and remove Tuanku Muhriz as Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Aug 7 Ten assemblymen from BN and PN are sworn in as Negeri Sembilan exco members, comprising seven from Umno and one each from MCA, PAS and Wawasan.

Sept 5 In a statement, the four “undangs” reveal that Ismail had signed the proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz. The following day, the menteri besar sidesteps the claim but declares full loyalty for Tuanku Muhriz.
Sept 8 The “undangs” hold a press conference and produce the purported proclamation signed by the menteri besar.
Sept 9 Ismail claims he signed the document “unwillingly and under coercion”, and maintains that the proclamation is invalid. He also lodges a police report to allow the matter to be probed.
Sept 16 The Negeri Sembilan exco members issue a statement claiming that Tuanku Muhriz’s removal in April was legitimate, and that Tunku Nadzaruddin was, therefore, the new ruler.

Sept 17 Ismail endorses the exco’s statement and orders the state secretary to proceed with gazetting the proclamation. However, the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) says the announcement has no legal effect as the menteri besar and exco have no authority to remove the ruler. The DKU also affirm that Tuanku Muhriz remains the rightful ruler.
Sept 18 Citing the AGC’s statement, the state secretary refuses to gazette the proclamation on Tuanku Muhriz’s removal.

Sept 20 Tuanku Muhriz moves to revoke the appointments of the exco members, except Ismail, with immediate effect. The palace says the 10 assemblymen violated their oaths of office and pledge of allegiance before the Yang Dipertuan Besar on Aug 7.
Sept 21 Ismail disputes the sacking of his exco members, arguing that the ruler cannot terminate their tenure unless advised or requested by the menteri besar.
Sept 22 Ismail says the exco has decided to suspend the state secretary and state legal adviser, with two interim replacements announced. However, the AGC says the exco has no authority to do so.
Sept 23 A meeting between the menteri besar, his former exco members and Tunku Nadzaruddin is called off amid heavy police presence. For the state secretary, it’s business as usual.

Sept 24 The 10 sacked exco members are barred from entering their offices following their sackings, but Ismail contends that they remain in their posts. Later that day, the revocation of their appointments is officially gazetted.
Sept 25 Rais claims trial to sedition in connection with the purported proclamation of a new Negeri Sembilan Yang Dipertuan Besar.

Sept 26 Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar affirms the revocation of the 10 exco members, saying the state constitution states that an exco member other than the menteri besar holds their post at the pleasure of the Yang Dipertuan Besar.
A source tells FMT that Bukit Aman will question the 10 former exco members over the crisis. The inspector-general of police confirms this the next day.
Sept 27 Calls grow for Ismail to resign as menteri besar, with the G25 group of prominent retired civil servants citing his frequent changes in stance in handling the crisis.

BN chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi orders Ismail to seek an audience with Tuanku Muhriz and the four undangs to resolve the crisis amicably. Zahid also holds a meeting with all 25 BN and PN assemblymen at Umno’s headquarters at night.
e83fd4690d401095: PETALING JAYA: Krisis institusi diraja Negeri Sembilan yang tercetus pada April berlarutan hampir enam bulan, dengan kebuntuan semakin meruncing selepas PRN 1 Ogos hingga kini disifatkan sebagai krisis perlembagaan.

Menteri besar ketika itu, Aminuddin Harun, menolak tindakan berkenaan dengan berkata Mubarak Dohak khususnya telah pun dilucutkan sebagai Undang Luak Sungai Ujong kerana melanggar undang-undang adat.
Penyingkiran Mubarak disahkan DKU, badan adat tertinggi negeri, pada 17 April.
27 April
Umno menarik balik sokongan terhadap Aminuddin susulan cara beliau menangani krisis itu, sekali gus menyebabkan pentadbiran menteri besar berada dalam keadaan tidak menentu.

Bagaimanapun, ura-ura pertukaran kerajaan reda selepas Bersatu menarik diri daripada menyokong pembentukan kerajaan antara BN-Perikatan Nasional (PN), sekali gus menyebabkan Umno gagal memperoleh majoriti mudah.
5 Mei
Empat individu terbabit memfailkan saman pemula bagi mendapatkan perintah mahkamah supaya kerajaan negeri dan DKU menyerahkan minit mesyuarat DKU pada 17 April yang mengesahkan penyingkiran Mubarak.
7 Mei
Pakatan Harapan (PH) dan Umno bersetuju melakukan ‘gencatan politik’, manakala Aminuddin terus menerajui kerajaan negeri.
13 Mei
DKU memohon untuk mencabar bidang kuasa Mahkamah Tinggi Seremban mendengar saman berkaitan krisis itu, atas alasan mahkamah tidak mempunyai bidang kuasa terhadap perkara berkenaan.
5 Jun
DUN dibubarkan selepas beberapa minggu ketegangan politik.
Mahkamah Tinggi kemudian membenarkan injunksi sementara bagi mengekalkan keadaan sedia ada di Negeri Sembilan ketika krisis adat dan perlembagaan itu berterusan.

Pada hari sama, Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar 'diisytiharkan' sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar ‘baharu’ oleh seorang daripada individu yang mendakwa dirinya undang dalam satu acara di hotel lima bintang di Melaka.
Bekas menteri besar Rais Yatim antara yang hadir dan mendakwa Negeri Sembilan kini mempunyai pemerintah baharu.
Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim pula berkata kerajaan persekutuan kekal mengiktiraf Tuanku Muhriz sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan.
9 Jun
Istana Negeri Sembilan berkata pengisytiharan Yang Dipertuan Besar ‘baharu’ itu tidak sah dan melucutkan gelaran warisan Tunku Panglima Besar daripada Tunku Nadzaruddin.
23 Jun
Mesyuarat Majlis Raja-Raja ditangguhkan, dilaporkan susulan krisis di Negeri Sembilan.
Raja-raja dikatakan mahu perkara itu diselesaikan oleh Yang Dipertuan Besar tanpa dibawa ke mahkamah.
25 Jun
Aktivis Badrul Hisham Shaharin, yang kemudiannya menjadi ketua Wawasan Negeri Sembilan, mengaku tidak bersalah atas pertuduhan menerbitkan bahan menghasut berkaitan institusi diraja Negeri Sembilan.
8 Julai
DKU mendapat kebenaran memulakan prosiding menghina mahkamah terhadap enam individu, termasuk empat ‘undang’ terbabit, kerana didakwa melanggar injunksi interim yang dikeluarkan pada 5 Jun.
Prosiding itu kemudian ditangguhkan sementara oleh Mahkamah Rayuan.
17 Julai
Empat ‘undang’ memfailkan permohonan semakan kehakiman bagi mendapatkan perintah mahkamah supaya Aminuddin menandatangani pengisytiharan yang kononnya menyingkirkan Tuanku Muhriz.
Pada 10 Ogos, DKU memohon mencelah dalam kes itu bagi mencabar pengisytiharan berkenaan. Pengurusan kes seterusnya ditetapkan pada 7 Okt.
30 Julai
Tuanku Muhriz melucutkan darjah kebesaran negeri yang dikurniakan kepada Rais.
1 Ogos
DKU mendedahkan tiga daripada empat ‘undang’ yang cuba menyingkirkan pemerintah negeri pada 19 April sebenarnya bukan undang ketika itu.
Menurut DKU, dua daripada mereka telah pun dipecat manakala seorang lagi tidak pernah dilantik secara rasmi, sekali gus menegaskan kedudukan Tuanku Muhriz sebagai pemerintah yang sah.
Pada malam sama, gabungan BN-PN memperoleh majoriti dua pertiga dalam PRN bagi membentuk kerajaan negeri baharu.
2 Ogos
Adun tujuh penggal daripada Umno, Ismail Lasim, mengangkat sumpah sebagai menteri besar di hadapan Tuanku Muhriz.
Pelantikannya disifatkan mengejutkan kerana beliau sebelum itu tidak disebut antara calon utama bagi jawatan berkenaan.
6 Ogos
Ketua Umno Negeri Sembilan Jalaluddin Alias menolak dakwaan beliau mahu menggulingkan Ismail sebagai menteri besar dan menyingkirkan Tuanku Muhriz sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar.
7 Ogos
Seramai 10 Adun BN dan PN mengangkat sumpah sebagai exco Negeri Sembilan, terdiri daripada tujuh wakil Umno serta masing-masing seorang daripada MCA, PAS dan Wawasan.
5 Sept
Dalam satu kenyataan, empat ‘undang’ mendakwa Ismail telah menandatangani pengisytiharan untuk menyingkirkan Tuanku Muhriz.
Keesokan harinya, Ismail tidak menjawab secara langsung dakwaan itu tetapi menegaskan taat setia sepenuhnya kepada Tuanku Muhriz.
8 Sept
Empat ‘undang’ itu mengadakan sidang media dan menunjukkan dokumen pengisytiharan yang didakwa ditandatangani menteri besar.
9 Sept
Ismail mendakwa beliau menandatangani dokumen itu 'di bawah paksaan' serta menegaskan pengisytiharan berkenaan tidak sah.
Beliau turut membuat laporan polis supaya perkara itu disiasat.
16 Sept
Ahli exco Negeri Sembilan mengeluarkan kenyataan mendakwa penurunan takhta Tuanku Muhriz pada April adalah sah dan dakwa Tunku Nadzaruddin sebagai pemerintah baharu negeri.
17 Sept
Ismail menyokong kenyataan exco itu dan mengarahkan setiausaha kerajaan negeri meneruskan proses mewartakan pengisytiharan berkenaan.
Bagaimanapun, Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) berkata pengumuman itu tidak mempunyai kesan undang-undang kerana menteri besar dan exco tidak mempunyai kuasa menyingkirkan Yang Dipertuan Besar.
DKU turut menegaskan Tuanku Muhriz kekal sebagai pemerintah yang sah.
18 Sept
Dengan merujuk kenyataan AGC, setiausaha kerajaan negeri enggan mewartakan pengisytiharan penyingkiran Tuanku Muhriz.
20 Sept
Tuanku Muhriz membatalkan pelantikan semua ahli exco kecuali Ismail berkuat kuasa serta-merta.
Istana berkata 10 Adun terbabit melanggar sumpah jawatan serta ikrar taat setia yang dibuat di hadapan Yang Dipertuan Besar pada 7 Ogos.
21 Sept
Ismail mempertikaikan penamatan khidmat anggota exconya dengan berhujah bahawa Yang Dipertuan Besar tidak boleh menamatkan jawatan mereka tanpa nasihat atau permintaan menteri besar.
22 Sept
Ismail berkata exco memutuskan untuk menggantung setiausaha kerajaan negeri dan penasihat undang-undang negeri, selain mengumumkan dua individu sebagai pengganti sementara.
Bagaimanapun, AGC berkata exco tidak mempunyai kuasa untuk berbuat demikian.
23 Sept
Pertemuan antara menteri besar, bekas ahli exconya dan Tunku Nadzaruddin dibatalkan di tengah-tengah kawalan ketat polis.
Sementara itu, setiausaha kerajaan negeri meneruskan tugas seperti biasa.
24 Sept
Sepuluh bekas ahli exco dihalang memasuki pejabat masing-masing susulan pembatalan pelantikan mereka, walaupun Ismail menegaskan mereka masih memegang jawatan.
c88000abdde91614: GAZA CITY: Gaza's Civil Defense said Sunday it had recovered the remains of 28 Palestinians from beneath the rubble of a house destroyed by the Israeli army in October 2023.
The remains were found at the Abu Naama family's residence in the Daraj neighbourhood of Gaza City, Anadolu Ajansi reported the agency said in a statement.
Family sources told Anadolu that Israeli warplanes had struck the house.

On Saturday, the Civil Defense said it recovered the remains of seven other Palestinians from two destroyed houses: one belonging to the Nuwairi family in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, and the other to the Atallah family in the Yarmouk area of Gaza City.
The recoveries are part of the second phase of the Civil Defense's project to retrieve the remains of people buried beneath buildings destroyed during Israel's war on Gaza.
The phase began on July 19 and covers sites in Gaza City, northern Gaza and the Nuseirat refugee camp.
The Civil Defense estimates 1,072 people may be beneath those buildings.
Teams plan to search 147 houses across Gaza's northern and central governorates over 800 working hours.
Civil Defense crews say the work is proceeding slowly because they lack the heavy equipment needed to clear the rubble.
Palestinian officials say the ceasefire agreement in effect since Oct. 10, 2025, provides for the entry of machinery to assist with debris removal and the recovery of victims.
In the first phase, which began in late November 2025, the remains of 333 people were recovered.

In October 2025, Gaza's government media office estimated that about 9,500 Palestinians were missing since the start of the war, including people believed to be buried under destroyed buildings and others whose whereabouts remained unknown.
The UN human rights office has also highlighted the continuing trauma caused by the long wait to recover the victims' remains. — BERNAMA
3768500bec13aaf4: OSLO: Goncalo Ramos started in place of Cristiano Ronaldo and scored the winner as Portugal made it back-to-back victories to start their UEFA Nations League title defence by beating Norway 2-1 in Oslo on Sunday.
Jorge Jesus's men have responded well to their tame World Cup last-16 loss to Spain, having also beaten Wales 1-0 in Group A4 on Thursday.

The 41-year-old Ronaldo was named among the substitutes for the first time for Portugal since a Nations League game against Scotland in September 2024, and did not get onto the pitch as Jesus looks to manage his minutes across an expanded international break.
World Cup quarter-finalists Norway were left to rue some wasteful finishing in front of goal as they failed to build on their opening 3-2 win over Denmark.

The first big chance fell to Erling Haaland, but the Manchester City striker mishit his attempted volley after being picked out by Martin Odegaard, and Portugal goalkeeper Diogo Costa was able to make the save.
The away team quickly made Haaland pay as Joao Felix stroked a fine finish into the bottom corner from the edge of the box in the 17th minute.
Haaland looked certain to equalise shortly afterwards when Costa spilled the ball into his path, but he was denied by a superb block from his City teammate Ruben Dias.
The Norway talisman was foiled by Costa again 10 minutes before half-time as the 'keeper made an excellent stop from his downward header.
Haaland finally converted six minutes into the second half, tapping in from Patrick Berg's header across goal.
But Norway gave back the lead immediately to their opponents, as goalkeeper Orjan Nyland passed the ball straight to Ramos, who coolly chipped it into the net.
Rafael Leao had a shot deflected onto the crossbar as Portugal pushed to make the game safe.
Nyland had his blushes spared when a VAR review ruled out another opportunistic Ramos effort for the tightest of offsides.
The 'keeper waited for a long pass over the top to reach him, then took a swipe at thin air as Ramos got to the ball before him and rolled it into an empty net.
Norway threw everyone forward, including Nyland, in the closing stages, but could not find another leveller.
a10423b53d927d5f: NEW YORK: Asean is being increasingly recognised as an important voice in addressing a wide range of global issues, with its position often awaited by the international community.

Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the regional bloc has emerged as an influential middle power, driven by consensus among its member states in voicing issues related to peace, human rights and compliance with international law.
"Asean's voice is now awaited by many countries and the international community because we speak as a united bloc.
"The world today is facing geopolitical and economic uncertainties. In such circumstances, the views put forward by Asean are receiving increasing attention," he said.
Mohamad said this to reporters at the conclusion of his working visit in conjunction with the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) here.
He said Asean, with a population of nearly 700 million, was now one of the fastest-growing economic regions in the world.
"By 2030, Asean is expected to become the world's fourth-largest economic power. That is why the international community is always looking to Asean for its views and positions," he said.
Mohamad, however, said Asean must continue to navigate its role carefully to ensure that the bloc remains neutral and is not perceived as siding with any particular power.
"We need to navigate this carefully because we do not want Asean to be seen as having any particular interests.
"What we voice are universal issues such as violations of human rights and international law," he said.
Mohamad said, when Asean voices a position, it represents the collective voice of its 11 member states, giving it greater strength and influence than acting alone.
This approach enables the bloc to continue playing a role as a bridge for dialogue and a trusted voice in addressing increasingly complex global challenges.
a8c7bbb7cd3307d1: SAN FRANCISO: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is set to dine one-on-one with President Donald Trump at the White House on Sunday evening, a tech industry source confirmed to AFP.
The meeting comes after months of open conflict between the artificial intelligence startup and the Trump administration.
The private dinner would be the first one-on-one meeting between the two men, according to US media including Axios, which first reported the dinner plan.
The invitation comes two days after a federal appeals court upheld the Pentagon's decision to classify Anthropic as a "supply chain risk," which prohibits the US military from using its models.
The startup had been sanctioned by the Trump administration after refusing in February to allow its tools to be used for fully autonomous weapons or domestic mass surveillance.
Trump also badmouthed Amodei, saying he was trying to be "a perfect little angel" after the Anthropic chief called for a pause in AI development.
Amodei was absent Thursday at the state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping attended by AI industry leaders, including Amodei rival Sam Altman of OpenAI.

Despite mounting calls to slow down AI development due to the risk of losing control of the technology, the US government believes that the sector's major players — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta -- cannot afford to slow down for fear that China will gain the upper hand.
Asked Sunday by Fox News about the numerous security incidents caused by advanced AI models, the president dismissed these concerns, saying "I'm not worried about it."
Trump and Mike Johnson, the speaker of the House of Representatives, are set to meet with leading AI executives on Tuesday.
0f206017787f51fd: SINGAPORE: Oil prices rebounded more than one per cent on Monday after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal from Iran to resolve their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent crude futures rose US$1.82, or 1.74 per cent, to US$106.14 a barrel by 2202 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$93.55 a barrel, up US$1.14, or 1.23 per cent.
9b451a72be8fd19f: NEW YORK: Iran wants Malaysia to continue playing the role of a mediating voice on the international stage by encouraging diplomatic efforts between Teheran and Washington to continue in order to ease tensions that continue to grip the Middle East.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia remains committed to diplomatic channels, which are an important foundation for preventing any crisis from escalating or dragging on.

"Iran wants peace negotiations to continue and hopes that the United States can view this matter from a different perspective in order to avoid a prolonged crisis," he told reporters at the conclusion of his working visit in conjunction with the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) here.
Mohamad had earlier held bilateral talks with his Iranian counterpart, Seyed Abbas Araghchi, on the sidelines of UNGA.
He said Araghchi also briefed him on the latest developments in the crisis affecting the region, as well as Teheran's continued commitment to a diplomatic solution.
At the same time, Mohamad said Malaysia expressed concern over the possibility of disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, which could have a significant impact on the regional economy.
"Malaysia hopes that the Strait of Hormuz will be reopened, as its closure has had a significant impact on many countries, particularly those in Asean.
"A large portion of the crude oil supplies shipped to the Asean region passes through the Strait of Hormuz, and any disruption would have far-reaching implications," he said.
He said Araghchi gave bhis assurances that Iran had no issue with ensuring that the route remains open if an agreement is reached and progress is made in ongoing diplomatic efforts.

Mohamad said, based on the discussion, Iran continues to prioritise a solution through diplomatic channels and is now awaiting a response to the proposals that have been put forward to allow negotiations to continue.
64dbda0ab060613c: MEDINAH: Top-ranked Scottie Scheffler was so aggravated by a yelling US supporter at the Presidents Cup on Sunday that he conceded a 30-foot chip shot to Colombia's Nico Echavarria.

The stand for sportsmanship took place on the 14th hole at Medinah late in the concluding singles matches of the event, which the United States won for the 11th consecutive time, beating the Internationals 17-13.

Scheffler owned a 3-up lead over the South American when a spectator in the crowd yelled as Echavarria was in the process of making his shot, the ball sailing well right as he glared at the disruptor.
Scheffler, a four-time major winner, walked toward the gallery and said, "There's no place for that."

To back up his point later on the hole, Scheffler conceded an unlikely chip shot and both players finished with a par on the hole, when Scheffler would likely have taken a 4-up lead with four holes remaining.
"It's just ridiculous, somebody yelling in his swing off the tee," Scheffler said after the match.
"There's absolutely no place for that. You should get 30 seconds to a minute when you're over the ball or getting ready to hit your shot where there's some silence, and it's just frustrating."
Echavarria praised Scheffler as a "class act" for his move.
"Someone yelled on my backswing. It didn't happen just once. It was a tough environment," he said.
"It's unfortunate that in some way the crowds can affect performance like that, but we have the number one player in the world, who is a class act.
"I wasn't expecting for him to give me that putt for par, and he did, and we tied the hole."
Scheffler, who defeated Echavarria 2&1 to finish 3-1 in Presidents Cup matches, said he was thrown off by the yell as well.
"I was very frustrated. It was honestly a big distraction, for me, just because we compete and work so hard to put ourselves in these moments," Scheffler explained.
"It just didn't really sit well with me. He would never hit a shot as poorly as he hit off the 14th if there wasn't a fan yelling in his swing. It was just very frustrating."
af8446bc04d15c36: AUGSBURG, Germany: Jurgen Klopp tasted defeat for the first time as Germany manager as his side lost 1-0 to Greece in Augsburg on Sunday, with Dimitrios Kourbelis scoring the only goal.

In his first game on home soil, Klopp's side offered little in attack and lacked the energy they had displayed on the former Liverpool coach's debut in a 1-1 away draw with the Netherlands on Thursday.
The Germans had struggled to find a way through the Greek defence for the opening hour before the visitors broke through on the counter, with Kourbelis scoring in the 74th minute.
It was Greece's first ever win against Germany.
"Personally, I'm completely unbothered by it. I've lost far more matches in my life than I would have liked," Klopp told ARD.
"But as long as you draw the right conclusions, a loss is ultimately just a piece of information – no different from a win.
"We absolutely need these kinds of matches – they are exactly the games we wanted to have."
Germany captain Joshua Kimmich added: "He's been very clear about what he wants – as players, we need to implement it."
'Very hyped'
Several regulars missed out with Klopp trying to get a better idea of the talent at his disposal, but the defeat illustrated the scale of his task in reviving the flagging giants.

The 59-year-old took over Germany in July after the four-time World Cup winners were eliminated at the last-32 stage of the global showpiece in North America, their third consecutive early exit from the tournament.
"I think the important thing is that we stand together and that won't change," said Germany centre-back Jonathan Tah.
"Of course, with the enthusiasm surrounding the new coach, things can get very hyped up from the outside, but ultimately, it comes down to what we do on the pitch and how we perform."
Klopp had included 16 uncapped players in his 44-man squad as he warned that he would be using the competition to have a look at the players at his disposal.
Among the five alterations to his starting XI was Hoffenheim forward Bambase Conte, a shock call-up after playing just four top-flight matches.
Conte looked sharp and shot just wide with two minutes gone.
Barcelona forward Karim Adeyemi had the best chance of the opening half when he stormed past the Greek defence on the counter, but sprayed his shot just over the crossbar.
Conte was again dangerous after the break, forcing a low fingertip save from Greek goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.

With Germany dominating possession but offering little in attack, the visitors grew bolder and more incisive on the counter and should have taken the lead when Fotis Ioannidis blasted wide of the goal with just Alexander Nuebel to beat.
Greece broke through moments later, however, when Kourbelis's low shot took a wicked deflection off Joshua Kimmich and rolled into the bottom left corner.
Greece then held firm for a breakthrough win over Germany, after seven defeats and three draws dating back to 1960.

In Kuala Lumpur, thunderstorms are expected in several areas this afternoon, while Putrajaya is forecast to remain fair and dry throughout the day.
Hulu Selangor and Gombak are expected to experience thunderstorms this afternoon and rain in several areas tonight, while rain is forecast for Petaling and Shah Alam this afternoon.
